queries.name: has_rider
queries.summary: Whether at least one entity is riding this entity
queries.hover:
1 if anything is riding the entity (any seat, player or mob), else 0.
Reads the entity's own passenger list; 0 without an entity. Arguments are ignored.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity carries at least one passenger, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while at least one entity sits on this entity - a player on a horse, a mob in a boat, a baby on a strider - and `0` otherwise. It does not matter which seat is used or how many passengers there are; use `query.rider_body_x_rotation` and similar queries for per-rider details.

The passenger list is shared with clients, so the value is the same in behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang. It changes the moment a passenger mounts or dismounts.

Without an entity it returns `0`. Arguments, if given, are ignored.

This is the mount's view; from the passenger's side use `query.is_riding`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

pitfalls: It is true for the mount, not the passenger - on the rider use `query.is_riding`.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: has_target
queries.summary: Whether a mob currently has an attack target
queries.hover:
1 while the mob has a target (the entity it is attacking or aiming at), else 0.
The target is shared with clients, so it works in resource packs too.
Non-mob entities (armor stands, boats) return 0; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the mob has a target entity - the one it is attacking, shooting at or pursuing - otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the mob has a target and `0` when it has none. The target is the entity the mob's AI has locked on to: what a skeleton aims at, what an iron golem attacks, what a fox stalks.

The game stores the target's identity on the entity and sends it to clients, so resource-pack animation controllers can switch poses on it (vanilla does this for skeletons, iron golems and foxes). The value changes when the AI picks or drops a target; it is `0` again once the target is cleared.

Only mobs have targets. Other entities (armor stands, boats) return `0`; expressions without an entity return `0`.

To know where the target is, combine it with `query.target_x_rotation` / `query.target_y_rotation`.

appliesTo.entities: mobs; other entities always 0

pitfalls: Only mobs pick targets; on non-mob entities (projectiles, boats, items) expect 0.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: head_is_in_water
queries.summary: Whether the entity's breathing point is inside water
queries.hover:
1 while the point the entity breathes from (about eye height) is inside water, else 0.
Lava and other liquids do not count. Updated once per tick; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity's head - the point it breathes from - is submerged in water, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity's breathing point is under water and `0` otherwise. The breathing point is the spot used for drowning checks, roughly at eye height; being waist-deep or swimming at the surface with the head out gives `0`.

Only water counts: lava gives `0`.

The game re-evaluates this once per tick as part of its water-state update, so the value switches on the tick the head goes under and off the tick it comes out. It is not smoothed between frames.

Without an entity the query returns `0`. For the whole body use `query.is_in_water`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity whose water state the game tracks

pitfalls: Swimming at the surface with the head above the water line reads 0.
Lava never counts.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: head_roll_angle
queries.summary: Wolf's sideways head tilt when interested, in radians (wolves only)
queries.hover:
Sideways head tilt of a wolf in radians: 0 when idle, up to about 0.47 (27 degrees) while interested.
Wolves only - every other entity returns 0. Multiply by 57.3 for degrees.
Eases towards its target by 40% per tick and is smoothed between frames.
queries.description: Returns how far a wolf tilts its head sideways - the 'interested' pose when you hold food near it - in radians. All other entities return 0.
queries.long:
Returns the roll of a wolf's head in **radians**. It is `0` while the wolf is not interested and rises towards `0.15 * pi` (about `0.471`, or 27 degrees) while it is (for example when a player holds food it likes nearby).

Every tick the tilt moves 40% of the remaining way towards its goal (`1` while interested, `0` otherwise), so it eases in and out over roughly half a second instead of snapping. The value you read is smoothed between the last two ticks with the frame's partial tick, and then scaled to radians:

`roll = lerp(previous, current, frame_alpha) * 0.15 * pi`

Bones rotate in degrees, so multiply by `57.3` before using it in a rotation.

Only wolves have this tilt. Every other entity, and expressions without an entity, return `0`.
queries.formula: `lerp(t_prev, t_now, frame_alpha) * 0.15 * pi`, with `t_now = t_prev + 0.4 * (goal - t_prev)` each tick, goal 1 while interested else 0

appliesTo.entities: wolves; every other entity 0

pitfalls: The result is in radians; used directly as a bone rotation it looks like no tilt at all.
Custom entities always get 0, even when they use the wolf's model or animations.
After interest ends it shrinks by 60% per tick but never becomes exactly 0 (values like 1e-20 remain); test against a small threshold, not `== 0`.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: head_x_rotation
queries.summary: Pitch of the entity (head 0) or of a wither's side head (1, 2), in degrees
queries.hover:
`q.head_x_rotation(head)` - pitch in degrees. 0: the entity's own pitch, smoothed between frames.
1 and 2 exist only on the wither (its two side heads, not smoothed); on other entities they log an error.
Index truncated toward zero (-0.5 reads head 0, -1 logs an error). Needs exactly one argument.
queries.description: Returns the up/down rotation (pitch) of a head in degrees. Index 0 is the entity's own pitch; the wither also has side heads 1 and 2.
queries.long:
Returns a head's pitch - how far it looks up or down - in degrees. Negative values look up, positive values look down.

| head | returns | who |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | the entity's own pitch, smoothed between ticks with the frame's partial tick | every entity |
| `1` | pitch of the wither's first side head (updated per tick, not smoothed) | wither only |
| `2` | pitch of the wither's second side head (updated per tick, not smoothed) | wither only |

Head `0` is the rotation of the entity as a whole, so for a single-headed mob it is simply where it looks. On a wither it is the centre head.

**Argument.** Exactly one number. The fractional part is dropped toward zero, so `-0.5` still reads head `0`, but `-1` and below are invalid. A negative index, `1` or `2` on anything other than a wither, and `3` or more on any entity write an error to the content log and return `0`; so does calling it with no argument or with more than one.

Without an entity the query returns `0` silently.

args.name: head
args.description: 0 = the entity itself; 1 and 2 = the wither's side heads
accepts: number; truncated toward zero (so -0.99 reads head 0)
args.onInvalid: -1 or below, 1-2 on a non-wither, or 3 or more: content-log error, returns 0

queries.range: pitch angle in degrees (about -90 to 90 for looking entities)

appliesTo.entities: any entity for head 0; heads 1-2 on the wither only

whenUnavailable.when: head 1 or 2 on an entity that is not a wither

pitfalls: Only head 0 is smoothed between frames; the wither's side heads (1, 2) step once per tick.
`q.head_x_rotation(1)` on a custom multi-headed entity logs an error - only the wither has extra heads.
`q.head_x_rotation(-1)` is an invalid index (error, 0); only fractions above -1 truncate to head 0.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: head_y_rotation
queries.summary: Yaw of a head in degrees; head turn relative to the body for horses (clamped)
queries.hover:
`q.head_y_rotation(arg)` - yaw in degrees. Horse family: head turn relative to the body, clamped to +-arg.
Others: arg is a head index like head_x_rotation (0 = entity yaw, wither also 1 and 2).
Non-horse head 0 is the entity's own world-space yaw; index truncated, -1 logs an error.
Needs exactly one argument; bad index or count logs an error and returns 0.
queries.description: Returns a head's left/right rotation (yaw) in degrees. For horses, donkeys, mules and skeleton/zombie horses the argument is a clamp and the result is the head turn relative to the body; for other entities the argument is a head index.
queries.long:
The argument means two different things depending on the entity.

**Horse family** (horse, donkey, mule, skeleton horse, zombie horse): the argument is a limit in degrees. The result is how far the head is turned away from the body, wrapped into `[-180, 180)` and then clamped to `[-limit, limit]`:

`clamp(wrap(head_yaw - body_yaw), -limit, limit)`

Both yaws are smoothed between ticks with the frame's partial tick. The limit is used as written - it is not rounded. Use a positive limit; a negative one flips the clamp and returns only the extreme values.

**Every other entity**: the argument is a head index, handled exactly like `query.head_x_rotation`:

| head | returns | who |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | the entity's own yaw in world space, smoothed between ticks | every entity |
| `1`, `2` | yaw of the wither's side heads (per tick, not smoothed) | wither only |

The index has its fractional part dropped toward zero; `-1` and below, `1`/`2` on a non-wither, and `3` and above write an error to the content log and return `0`. The wither's side-head yaws are world-space angles that are not wrapped, so values like `-430` occur.

Note that head `0` is a world-space angle: it changes when the entity turns around, and it is not the head turn relative to the body that the horse form gives you. For a look-at pose relative to the body, subtract `query.body_y_rotation` yourself.

Calling it with no argument or more than one logs an error and returns `0`; without an entity it returns `0` silently.

args.name: limit_or_head
args.description: Horse family: clamp in degrees. Others: head index (0; wither 0-2)
accepts: horse family: any number, used as is (positive expected)
others: number truncated toward zero; -1 or below invalid; 1-2 wither only
args.onInvalid: others: -1 or below, 1-2 on a non-wither, or 3 or more: content-log error, returns 0. A string argument is not rejected: it returns a meaningless near-zero number without an error

queries.formula: horse family: `clamp(wrapDegrees(head_yaw - body_yaw), -arg, arg)`; others: entity yaw (arg 0) or wither side-head yaw
queries.range: horse family: [-arg, arg]; others: yaw in degrees

appliesTo.entities: horse family reads a clamp; wither has heads 0-2; every other entity head 0 only

whenUnavailable.when: head 1 or 2 on an entity that is neither a wither nor horse family
head 3 or more on an entity that is not horse family

pitfalls: On a horse `q.head_y_rotation(0)` is always 0 - the argument is a clamp there, not a head index.
For non-horse entities head 0 is a world-space yaw; using it directly on a head bone doubles the body's turn.
A custom entity that uses a horse model but is not in the horse family gets the head-index behaviour.
A string argument is not rejected: it silently returns a meaningless near-zero number.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: health
queries.summary: Current health, rounded up to a whole number
queries.hover:
Current health points rounded up to a whole number (0.5 health reads 1). 0 when dead.
Boats, minecarts and items have no health and return 0; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns the entity's current health as a whole number, rounded up. Entities without a health value return 0.
queries.long:
Returns the entity's current health - one point is half a heart - as a whole number.

Health is stored with fractions, but this query rounds it **up**: `19.2` reads `20`, `0.5` reads `1`. Zero or negative health reads `0`. The maximum health is not involved; use it together with your own known maximum, as vanilla does for the iron golem's crack textures.

Entities that have no health value (boats, minecarts, items) return `0`; an armor stand does have health (`6`). An expression without an entity returns `0`.

Health is shared with clients, so the value is available in resource-pack Molang. It changes whenever the entity is damaged or healed.
queries.formula: `ceil(h)` for `h > 0`, else `0`

appliesTo.entities: entities with health (mobs, players); others 0

pitfalls: The value is rounded up: comparisons like `q.health < 1` are only true at exactly 0.
It is the current health, not a fraction of the maximum.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: heartbeat_interval
queries.summary: Time between heartbeats in seconds (warden-style heartbeat)
queries.hover:
Seconds between the entity's heartbeats (ticks / 20): calm warden 2, angry warden 0.5.
Every other entity reads 1 in resource packs (a default 20-tick beat), not 0.
Without an entity it logs an error and returns 0.
queries.description: Returns the current time between the entity's heartbeats in seconds. The warden's follows its anger; every other entity reads a default of 1 in resource packs.
queries.long:
Returns how long one heartbeat lasts, in seconds. The interval is kept in ticks and divided by `20`, so a 40-tick beat reads `2` and the result moves in steps of `0.05`.

The interval comes from the entity's heartbeat component, which evaluates its own Molang expression (the warden speeds its heart up as it gets angrier). The number is shared with clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang see the same value.

Entities without a heartbeat definition do not read `0`: in resource-pack Molang they read `1` (a default 20-tick beat) - zombies, armor stands, boats and players all do. So `q.heartbeat_interval > 0` does not tell you whether an entity has a heartbeat. Running the query without an entity writes an error to the content log and returns `0`.

To animate a pulse, `query.heartbeat_phase` gives the position inside the current beat (resource packs only).
queries.formula: `interval_ticks / 20`
queries.range: 0 and up, steps of 0.05 (1 by default)

appliesTo.entities: warden (anger-dependent); every other entity reads the default 1 in resource packs

whenUnavailable.when: entity has no heartbeat definition (resource packs)

timing.updates: on change of the heartbeat interval

pitfalls: It is in seconds, not ticks: multiply by 20 to compare with tick counts.
Entities without a heartbeat read 1, not 0, in resource packs.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: heartbeat_phase
queries.summary: Position inside the current heartbeat, 0 to 1 (resource packs only)
queries.hover:
Progress through the current heartbeat: 0 on the beat, rising linearly to 1, then back to 0.
Client only: in behavior packs it logs an error and returns 0.
Steps once per tick; entities without a heartbeat cycle too, on a default 1 s beat.
queries.description: Returns a 0-to-1 fraction that climbs steadily between two of the entity's heartbeats and resets on each beat. Only resource-pack (client) Molang can read it.
queries.long:
Returns the entity's position inside its current heartbeat as a fraction.

The client keeps its own beat clock for every entity with a heartbeat: when a beat happens it plays the heartbeat sound and restarts the count. Each tick the phase is

`phase = clamp(ticks_since_last_beat / interval_ticks, 0, 1)`

so it rises in equal steps of `1 / interval_ticks`, holds `1` for one tick and drops back to `0` on the next tick. A full cycle therefore lasts `interval_ticks + 1` ticks - 41 for a calm warden, 21 at the default interval. It is not smoothed between frames; with a short interval the steps are visible. The interval is the one `query.heartbeat_interval` reports.

**Client only.** The beat clock exists only on clients: evaluated in behavior-pack Molang the query writes an error to the content log and returns `0`. Without an entity it also logs an error. Entities without a heartbeat definition are not `0`: the client runs the same clock for them at the default 1-second interval, so zombies, armor stands, boats and players all cycle from `0` to `1`.
queries.formula: `clamp((now_tick - last_beat_tick) / interval_ticks, 0, 1)`; 0 when the interval is 0

appliesTo.entities: warden; every other entity cycles at the default 1 s interval

pitfalls: Behavior-pack Molang gets 0 plus a content-log error.
It steps once per tick, so a pulse driven by it is not frame-smooth.
On a live entity it is never constantly 0: entities without a heartbeat pulse once a second.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22

queries.name: heightmap
queries.summary: Terrain height of the world column at (x, z) - world generation only
queries.hover:
`q.heightmap(x, z)` - height recorded for the column at x, z (coordinates rounded to whole blocks).
World-generation Molang only (feature and feature-rule expressions).
Needs exactly two arguments; otherwise returns 0 without an error.
queries.description: Returns the height stored for the world column at the given x and z. Available only in world-generation expressions.
queries.long:
Looks up the height the game keeps for every world column - the top of the terrain as seen from the sky - at the given x and z.

```
"y": "q.heightmap(v.worldx, v.worldz)"
```

Both coordinates are rounded to the nearest whole block (halves round away from zero: `0.5` becomes `1`, `-0.5` becomes `-1`). The result is a whole number: the first free y above the column's top block (one more than the top block's y). Blocks that let light through, such as glass, are skipped.

If the column's chunk is not available the query returns the dimension's lowest height instead of an error.

This query exists only for world generation: scatter parameters of features, `conditional_list` conditions and the other `world_gen` Molang fields. It does not resolve in entity, block or resource-pack Molang.

It needs exactly two arguments; any other count returns `0` silently.

args.name: x
args.description: World X
accepts: number; rounded to nearest, halves away from zero

args.name: z
args.description: World Z
accepts: number; rounded to nearest, halves away from zero

whenUnavailable.when: no world access in the context

pitfalls: Wrong argument count is silent: `q.heightmap(v.worldx)` is simply 0.
The value is one above the top block: placing something at `q.heightmap(x, z)` puts it on the surface, not in it.
Glass and other see-through blocks are skipped, so a feature can land under a glass roof.

queries.name: hurt_direction
queries.summary: Wobble direction of a hit boat, minecart or armor stand (1 or -1)
queries.hover:
Direction of the hit wobble on boats, minecarts and armor stands: 1 or -1, flipping with every hit.
Every other entity (mobs and players included) returns 0. 0 without an entity.
queries.description: For boats, minecarts and armor stands, returns the side the next hit wobble swings to: `1` or `-1`, flipping on every hit. Other entities return 0.
queries.long:
Boats, minecarts and armor stands rock when they are hit. This query returns which way that rock goes: `1` or `-1`. The sign flips on every hit, so consecutive hits rock the object back and forth. It says nothing about where the attacker was.

Use it together with `query.hurt_time`, which counts down how long the rock lasts - vanilla minecart animations multiply the two.

No other entity keeps this value: mobs and players return `0`, as do expressions without an entity.

appliesTo.entities: boats, minecarts, armor stands; every other entity 0

whenUnavailable.when: entity is not a boat, minecart or armor stand

pitfalls: It is not the direction the damage came from.
Mobs always return 0.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: hurt_time
queries.summary: Hit-wobble countdown of boats, minecarts, armor stands and the warden (ticks)
queries.hover:
Ticks left of the hit reaction: set to 10 on a hit and counted down by 1 per tick.
Kept only by boats, minecarts, armor stands and the warden; other mobs and players always return 0.
Whole numbers, not smoothed (vanilla subtracts q.frame_alpha itself).
queries.description: For boats, minecarts, armor stands and the warden, returns how many ticks of the hit reaction are left: 10 right after a hit, counting down to 0. Every other entity returns 0.
queries.long:
Returns a countdown in ticks that starts at `10` when the entity is hit and goes down by `1` each tick until it reaches `0`.

Only a few entity types keep this number:

| entity | what drives it |
|---|---|
| boats, minecarts | set to 10 by each hit; the wobble animation |
| armor stands | the wobble after a hit |
| warden | copied every tick from its hurt timer (the red flash) |

Every other entity - ordinary mobs and players included - returns `0`, even while it is flashing red from damage. There is no general "was just hurt" query for mobs.

The value is a whole number that changes once per tick. Vanilla minecarts smooth it themselves with `query.hurt_time - query.frame_alpha`.

Combine with `query.hurt_direction` for the side of the wobble. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: boats, minecarts, armor stands, warden; every other entity 0

whenUnavailable.when: entity type does not keep a hurt countdown (most mobs, players)

pitfalls: On ordinary mobs and players it is always 0 - it cannot detect that a zombie or a player was just hit.
It counts ticks, not seconds.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: in_range
queries.summary: Whether a value lies between a minimum and a maximum (both inclusive)
queries.hover:
`q.in_range(value, min, max)` - 1 if min <= value <= max, else 0.
Needs no entity and works in every context. min greater than max is always 0.
The max argument is not evaluated when value < min; wrong count or a string argument logs an error.
queries.description: Returns 1 when `value` is at least `min` and at most `max`, otherwise 0. Both ends count as inside.
queries.long:
Checks `min <= value <= max` and returns `1` or `0`.

```
q.in_range(q.time_of_day, 0.25, 0.75)
```

Both bounds are inclusive. The bounds are not reordered: if `min` is larger than `max`, nothing is in range and the result is always `0`.

**Evaluation order.** The arguments are evaluated left to right, and the check stops early: when `value` is below `min` the result is `0` and `max` is never evaluated (so side effects or errors in it do not happen).

**Errors.** Exactly three arguments are required, and each one that is evaluated must be a number. A wrong count or a string argument writes an error to the content log and returns `0`.

The query uses no entity or block data, so it works in every entity, particle and block context.

args.name: value
args.description: Value to test
args.onInvalid: string: content-log error, returns 0

args.name: min
args.description: Lower bound (inclusive)
args.onInvalid: string: content-log error, returns 0

args.name: max
args.description: Upper bound (inclusive); only evaluated when value >= min
args.onInvalid: string: content-log error, returns 0 (only if reached)

queries.formula: `min <= value && value <= max`

appliesTo.entities: no entity needed

whenUnavailable.when: an evaluated argument is not a number

pitfalls: Bounds are not swapped for you: `q.in_range(5, 10, 0)` is 0.
An error in the third argument goes unnoticed while value < min, because it is never evaluated.
A NaN value (for example `math.sqrt(-1)`) counts as in range and returns 1.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: invulnerable_ticks
queries.summary: Wither's remaining summoning-invulnerability ticks (wither only)
queries.hover:
Ticks left of the wither's invulnerable charge-up after it is summoned; 0 once it is over.
Wither only - every other entity returns 0. Not the brief immunity after taking damage.
queries.description: Returns how many ticks remain of the wither's invulnerable phase after it is summoned. Every other entity returns 0.
queries.long:
A freshly summoned wither spends its first moments growing and cannot be hurt. This query returns how many ticks of that phase are left: it starts at about `200` (10 seconds), counts down by `1` per tick while the wither's health fills up, and stays `0` for the rest of the fight. The value is saved with the wither; that it survives reloading the world is not yet verified in game.

Vanilla uses it to flash the wither's texture near the end of the phase:

```
(q.invulnerable_ticks <= 80) && (math.mod(q.invulnerable_ticks / 5, 2) == 1)
```

Despite its name it is **not** the short damage immunity every mob gets after being hit; there is no query for that. Every entity other than the wither returns `0`, as do expressions without an entity.

appliesTo.entities: wither only; every other entity 0

pitfalls: Custom entities always get 0 - the value exists only on the wither.
It does not reflect the post-hit damage immunity of mobs.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_admiring
queries.summary: Whether the entity is admiring an item (piglin gold pose)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is admiring an item it picked up (the piglin's gold-inspecting pose), else 0.
Set by the admire-item behavior; shared with clients. 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is in its admiring state - the piglin looking at a piece of gold it was given - otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is admiring an item and `0` otherwise. The state is switched on and off by the admire-item behavior (`minecraft:admire_item`), which piglins use when they pick up gold.

The flag is synchronised to clients, so the same value is available in resource-pack animation controllers - vanilla uses it to suppress the piglin's attack poses while it inspects the gold.

Entities that never admire anything always return `0`, as does an expression without an entity.

appliesTo.entities: any entity; only ones with the admire-item behavior ever get 1

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_alive
queries.summary: Whether the entity is alive (mobs: health above 0)
queries.hover:
Mobs and players: 1 while health is above 0 and the entity has not been removed; 0 once it dies.
Other entities (items, boats, projectiles) are 1 for as long as they exist.
0 without an entity.
queries.description: For mobs and players, returns 1 while their health is above 0; it becomes 0 as soon as they die, during the death animation. Other entities count as alive until they are removed.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is alive and `0` otherwise. What "alive" means depends on the kind of entity:

| entity | alive when |
|---|---|
| mobs, players | not removed from the world **and** health above 0 |
| everything else (items, boats, minecarts, projectiles, ...) | not removed from the world |

For mobs this turns `0` at the moment of death, so it is `0` throughout the death animation and, for players, while the respawn screen is shown. Health is checked after rounding up, so any fraction of a point still counts as alive.

Non-mob entities have no health to lose; for them the value is `1` in any expression that can still see them.

Without an entity the query returns `0`.
queries.formula: mobs: `!removed && ceil(health) > 0`; others: `!removed`

appliesTo.entities: any entity (meaning differs for mobs, see table)

pitfalls: For non-mob entities it is effectively always 1.
It is already 0 during a mob's death animation, so it cannot be used to keep a pose while the body falls over.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_angry
queries.summary: Whether the entity is angry (has the minecraft:angry state active)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity's anger state is on, else 0.
Driven by the `minecraft:angry` component (wolves, bees, endermen, piglins, ...); other entities read 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is in its angry state, which the `minecraft:angry` component switches on and off. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is angry and `0` otherwise.

The state belongs to the `minecraft:angry` component: it turns on when the component makes the entity angry (for example after it is hurt, or when an ally broadcasts anger) and turns off when the anger runs out or the component is removed. Removing the component group that holds `minecraft:angry` clears the flag. The state is also saved with the entity, so an angry mob is still angry after the world reloads.

Entities without that component - including every entity in vanilla that never gets angry - always read `0`.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with the minecraft:angry component; others always 0

pitfalls: Nothing but the `minecraft:angry` component sets this flag: an entity that simply targets or attacks you (a zombie, a skeleton) reads 0.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_attached
queries.summary: Whether the expression is running for an attachable (held or worn item model)
queries.hover:
1 when evaluated while an attachable (a held or worn item model) is being set up for drawing, else 0.
Resource packs only: on the server it writes a content-log error and returns 0.
Outside entity rendering it reads 0 without a log; the in-render values are not yet verified.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the expression is being evaluated for an attachable - the model drawn for an item an entity holds or wears - and 0 otherwise. Resource-pack Molang only.
queries.long:
Tells an expression whether it is running as part of an attachable: the item model that the client draws on an entity for a held or worn item. When the client prepares an attachable for drawing it marks the evaluation as attached, and this query reads that mark, returning `1`.

Anywhere else - an entity's own animations and render controllers, particles - the mark is not set and the result is expected to be `0`. Evaluated for an entity outside entity rendering it reads `0` without a log; the values inside an attachable and inside the entity's own render pass are not yet verified in game.

**Resource packs only.** The query first checks that it is running on a client. In behavior-pack (server) Molang it writes an error to the content log and returns `0`. Without an entity it also writes an error and returns `0`.

This is unrelated to `query.is_attached_to_entity`, which describes a firework rocket fastened to a gliding player.

appliesTo.entities: any entity; 1 only while drawing an attachable

timing.updates: per frame (set while the attachable is prepared)

pitfalls: Using it in a behavior pack is not silent: every evaluation writes a content-log error.
It says nothing about riding, leashing or firework rockets - use `query.is_riding`, `query.is_leashed` or `query.is_attached_to_entity` for those.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_attached_to_entity
queries.summary: Whether a firework rocket is fastened to an entity (elytra boost)
queries.hover:
1 when the entity is a firework rocket that is fastened to an entity - the rocket boosting a gliding player.
Every other entity type always reads 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 for a firework rocket that is attached to an entity, as when a player uses a rocket to boost while gliding. Every other entity type returns 0.
queries.long:
Only firework rockets can answer this query. A rocket used while gliding with elytra is fastened to the player instead of flying freely; for such a rocket the query returns `1` (not yet verified in game). A free-flying rocket returns `0`.

For any entity that is not a firework rocket - including the gliding player itself - the result is always `0`. Riding, leashing and held items are not considered.

The link to the boosted entity is synchronised to clients, so the value is the same in behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: firework rockets only; every other entity 0

whenUnavailable.when: entity is not a firework rocket

pitfalls: It is not a general "is riding / is leashed" test: on anything but a firework rocket it is always 0.
The gliding player does not read 1 - only the rocket does.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_avoiding_block
queries.summary: Whether the entity is running away from a block
queries.hover:
1 while the entity's avoid-block behavior is running (e.g. a hoglin fleeing warped fungus), else 0.
Set only by `minecraft:behavior.avoid_block`; entities without it always read 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is fleeing from a block because its `minecraft:behavior.avoid_block` goal is active, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` for exactly as long as the entity's `minecraft:behavior.avoid_block` behavior is running: the flag is switched on when the behavior starts fleeing and off when it stops. In vanilla that is the hoglin fleeing warped fungus and the piglin fleeing soul fire and similar blocks.

Only this behavior sets the flag; entities without it always read `0`.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities using minecraft:behavior.avoid_block; others always 0

pitfalls: Fleeing from a mob is a separate flag: use `query.is_avoiding_mobs` for `minecraft:behavior.avoid_mob_type`.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_avoiding_mobs
queries.summary: Whether the entity is running away from other mobs
queries.hover:
1 while the entity's avoid-mob behavior is running (e.g. a villager fleeing a zombie), else 0.
Set only by `minecraft:behavior.avoid_mob_type`; entities without it always read 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is fleeing from another mob because its `minecraft:behavior.avoid_mob_type` goal is active, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` for exactly as long as the entity's `minecraft:behavior.avoid_mob_type` behavior is running: the flag is switched on when the behavior starts and off when it stops. Many vanilla mobs use this behavior (villagers, cats, rabbits, fish, skeletons fleeing wolves, creepers fleeing cats, ...).

Only this behavior sets the flag; running away for other reasons (panic after being hurt, for example) does not.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities using minecraft:behavior.avoid_mob_type; others always 0

pitfalls: Panic (`minecraft:behavior.panic`) is not avoidance: a mob fleeing after being hit reads 0 here.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_baby
queries.summary: Whether the entity is a baby
queries.hover:
1 if the entity is flagged as a baby, else 0.
Works in resource and behavior packs; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity carries the baby flag, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the entity is a baby and `0` otherwise.

The flag comes from the entity's definition (the `minecraft:is_baby` component, usually added by a component group while the mob grows up) and is synchronised to clients, so the same value is seen in behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang. It takes no arguments; without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22

queries.name: is_breathing
queries.summary: Whether the entity is breathing (not running out of air underwater)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity can breathe where it is; 0 while it cannot and its head is in water.
Updated each tick for living mobs with `minecraft:breathable`; others keep 0.
Creative players, water breathing and fish on land read 1; survival players read 0 as soon as the head is under.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity can breathe at its current position and 0 while it cannot breathe with its head in water, as decided every tick from its `minecraft:breathable` component.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity can breathe and `0` while it is running out of air underwater.

Every tick, for each living mob that has `minecraft:breathable`, the game looks at the block at the entity's eyes and decides whether the entity can breathe there (using the component's `breathes_air`, `breathes_water`, `breathes_solids`, `breathes_lava` and the `breathe_blocks` / `non_breathe_blocks` lists). When it can, the flag is `1`. When it cannot and its head is in water, the flag is `0` from the first tick - the air supply does not have to run low first.

Some special cases:

| situation | value |
|---|---|
| player in creative mode, head under water | `1` |
| player with the water breathing effect, head under water | `1` |
| turtle under water | `1` |
| rider of a mount that lets riders breathe underwater, while submerged | `1` (expected) |
| player with the invulnerable ability (not creative) | not updated - keeps its last value (expected) |
| entity without `minecraft:breathable` | never set - `0` |
| dead entity | not updated - keeps its last value (expected) |

The rows marked expected are not yet verified in game. When the entity cannot breathe and its head is **not** in water the flag stays `1`: a cod flopping on land reads `1` while it suffocates (a mob with its head inside a solid block is expected to behave the same).

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: living mobs with minecraft:breathable (includes players); others always 0

pitfalls: Entities without `minecraft:breathable` read 0, which looks like "not breathing" - check the component, not just the value.
A fish on land reads 1 even though it is suffocating - the flag only reports running out of air in water.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_bribed
queries.summary: Whether the entity has been bribed (minecraft:bribeable)
queries.hover:
1 after the entity accepted a bribe through `minecraft:bribeable` (a dolphin fed raw fish), else 0.
Cleared again when the bribe wears off; entities without the component read 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 once the entity has accepted a bribe through its `minecraft:bribeable` component (in vanilla, a dolphin fed fish), until the bribe is reset. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` after the entity has been bribed and `0` otherwise.

The flag belongs to the `minecraft:bribeable` component: it is set when a player feeds the entity one of the component's `bribe_items`, and cleared when the component resets the bribe. A bribed entity keeps the flag across a world reload. In vanilla only the dolphin is bribeable.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:bribeable (dolphin in vanilla); others always 0

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_carrying_block
queries.summary: Whether the entity holds a block item (older files: endermen only)
queries.hover:
1 if the item in the entity's main hand is a block item, else 0.
Files at Molang version 1.21.100 or newer: any entity - a player holding dirt reads 1.
Older files: only endermen can read 1 (the carried block, air excluded).
queries.description: Returns 1 when the item the entity carries in its main hand is a block. The answer depends on the Molang version of the file: newer files accept any entity, older files only endermen.
queries.long:
Looks at the item the entity carries - the main hand for mobs, the selected hotbar slot for players - and returns `1` if it is a block item.

The rules changed with Molang version 1.21.100 (the file's `format_version` decides which rules apply):

| file version | who can read 1 | test |
|---|---|---|
| 1.21.100 and newer | any entity | carried item is a block item |
| older | endermen only | carried item is a block item and that block is not air |

So with a current file a player holding a stack of dirt, a zombie picking up a block item or an enderman carrying grass all read `1`, while with an older file only the enderman does and every other entity reads `0`.

Items that place blocks without being block items themselves do not count: wheat seeds, a bucket and sugar cane all read `0`. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity holding an item (1.21.100+ files); endermen only in older files

whenUnavailable.when: older file version and the entity is not an enderman
empty hand or a non-block item

pitfalls: With a 1.21.100+ file it is no longer an enderman-only query: players and mobs holding any block item read 1.
Raising a file's `format_version` past 1.21.100 changes the result for non-enderman entities without any other edit.
Seeds, buckets and sugar cane place blocks but are not block items, so holding them reads 0.

behaviourChangesByVersion.change: Endermen only: 1 when the carried item is a block item whose block is not air; every other entity 0.
Any entity: 1 when the carried (main-hand) item is a block item.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_casting
queries.summary: Whether the entity is casting a spell (evoker-style behaviors)
queries.hover:
1 while a spell-casting behavior is running (evoker summoning vexes or fangs, turning sheep), else 0.
Set by `minecraft:behavior.send_event` and `minecraft:behavior.summon_entity`; others read 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is in the middle of a spell cast from `minecraft:behavior.send_event` or `minecraft:behavior.summon_entity` (the evoker's behaviors), otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is casting and `0` otherwise.

Two behaviors turn the flag on when they start a cast and off when the cast finishes or is interrupted: `minecraft:behavior.summon_entity` (the evoker's fangs and vexes) and `minecraft:behavior.send_event` (the evoker turning a blue sheep red). In vanilla only the evoker uses them.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities using minecraft:behavior.send_event or minecraft:behavior.summon_entity; others always 0

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_celebrating
queries.summary: Whether the entity is celebrating (after a raid or a successful hunt)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is celebrating, else 0.
Raiders and villagers after a raid (`minecraft:behavior.celebrate`, `celebrate_survive`), piglins after a kill (`minecraft:celebrate_hunt`).
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is celebrating: raiders or villagers at the end of a raid, or a piglin after its hunt succeeded. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is celebrating and `0` otherwise. Three mechanisms set it:

| source | who in vanilla | when |
|---|---|---|
| `minecraft:behavior.celebrate` | pillagers, vindicators, evokers, witches, ravagers | while the behavior runs (raid won) |
| `minecraft:behavior.celebrate_survive` | villagers | while the behavior runs (raid survived) |
| `minecraft:celebrate_hunt` | piglins | after killing a target that matches the component's filters, for the component's duration |

A hunt celebration is the ordinary one nine times in ten; the tenth time the entity does the special celebration instead, which `query.is_celebrating_special` reports and this query does not.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with the celebrate behaviors or minecraft:celebrate_hunt; others always 0

pitfalls: A piglin's hunt celebration sets either this flag or `query.is_celebrating_special`, never both; check both if you want "any celebration".

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; not yet verified in game

queries.name: is_celebrating_special
queries.summary: Whether the entity is doing its rare special hunt celebration
queries.hover:
1 while the entity does the special version of a hunt celebration (`minecraft:celebrate_hunt`), else 0.
Each hunt celebration has a 1-in-10 chance to be the special one; piglins only in vanilla.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity performs the special variant of its hunt celebration from `minecraft:celebrate_hunt`, otherwise 0. One celebration in ten is special.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is doing its special celebration and `0` otherwise.

When an entity with `minecraft:celebrate_hunt` kills a matching target it starts celebrating for the component's duration. The kind of celebration is rolled once per kill: with a 1-in-10 chance it is the special one (this query), otherwise the ordinary one (`query.is_celebrating`). Allies that join the celebration through the component's broadcast get the same kind. The flag is cleared when the duration runs out.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:celebrate_hunt (piglins in vanilla); others always 0

pitfalls: Raid celebrations never set this flag - only hunt celebrations can be special.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; not yet verified in game

queries.name: is_charged
queries.summary: Whether the entity's charged state is on (loaded crossbow, blaze attack)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity's charged state is on, else 0.
Set by `minecraft:behavior.charge_held_item` (pillager/piglin loading a crossbow) and by ranged attacks that charge up (blaze). Not the creeper's charged state - that is `query.is_powered`.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity's charged state is on - a pillager or piglin holding a loaded crossbow, or a blaze powering up its fireballs - otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is charged and `0` otherwise. Two things turn the state on:

- `minecraft:behavior.charge_held_item` - a pillager or piglin loading its crossbow; the state stays on while the crossbow is loaded, and a pillager saves it with the world.
- `minecraft:behavior.ranged_attack` with a charge-up (`charge_charged_trigger` / `charge_shoot_trigger`) - the blaze while it powers up and fires (about 1.3 seconds on, then off until the next volley); the blaze shows its flames while charged. The ghast is charged for the short moment before each fireball.

A creeper struck by lightning is **not** charged in this sense; use `query.is_powered` for it.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: pillagers, piglins, blazes and other entities using those behaviors; others always 0

pitfalls: For a lightning-struck creeper this reads 0; the creeper uses `query.is_powered`.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_charging
queries.summary: Whether the entity is performing a charge attack (vex dash)
queries.hover:
1 while `minecraft:behavior.charge_attack` is running (the vex dashing at its target), else 0.
No other behavior was found to set it; drawing a bow is `query.is_using_item`.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is dashing at its target with `minecraft:behavior.charge_attack` (the vex in vanilla), otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is performing a charge attack and `0` otherwise.

The flag is switched on when `minecraft:behavior.charge_attack` starts a dash and off when the dash ends. In vanilla that behavior belongs to the vex. Vanilla also reads this query in the player, drowned and humanoid animation setups, but nothing else was found to set it: a pillager loading its crossbow and a drowned holding a trident at its target read `0`. Whether a player drawing a bow ever reads `1` is not yet verified.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities using minecraft:behavior.charge_attack (vex in vanilla); others expected 0

pitfalls: Drawing a bow or loading a crossbow is not "charging" here - use `query.is_using_item` or `query.is_charged`.

Returns `1` when the entity carries a chest and `0` otherwise.

The flag follows the `minecraft:is_chested` component: adding the component (vanilla does this through a component group when a player puts a chest on a donkey, mule or llama) sets it, and removing the component clears it. It is also saved with the entity.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

queries.name: is_cooldown_category
queries.summary: Whether the item in an equipment slot uses the given cooldown category
queries.hover:
`q.is_cooldown_category('category', 'slot.name', [index])` - 1 if the item in that slot has that cooldown category.
Index is required for hotbar, inventory, enderchest and chest slots; other slots ignore a third argument.
'' matches any item that has no cooldown category; an empty or missing slot reads 0.
queries.description: Checks the item in one equipment or inventory slot of the entity and returns 1 when that item's cooldown category equals the given name, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Compares the cooldown category of the item in one slot with a name.

```
q.is_cooldown_category('shield', 'slot.weapon.offhand')
q.is_cooldown_category('ender_pearl', 'slot.hotbar', 0)
```

**Category.** The first argument is the category name, compared exactly. Data-driven items take it from their `minecraft:cooldown` component's `category`. A few built-in items have a fixed category: the shield (`shield`), the goat horn (`goat_horn`) and the ender pearl (`ender_pearl`). An item without a category counts as having the empty name, so `''` matches every such item.

**Slot name.** The second argument is a slot name as used by `/replaceitem` (`slot.weapon.mainhand`, `slot.weapon.offhand`, `slot.armor.head`, ... ). An unknown name writes an error and returns `0`.

**Slot index.** `slot.hotbar`, `slot.inventory`, `slot.enderchest` and `slot.chest` need a third argument, the slot number (the fractional part is dropped). Leaving it out writes an error and returns `0`. For every other slot a third argument is ignored.

**Empty slots.** An empty slot returns `0` without an error, and so does an index out of range (`-1`, `99`).

Category names have no namespace and are case-sensitive: `'minecraft:shield'` and `'SHIELD'` do not match a shield.

The query only checks which category the item has; it does not tell you whether that category is cooling down right now.

args.name: category
args.description: Cooldown category name to compare with
accepts: '' matches items that have no cooldown category
args.onInvalid: not a string: content-log error, returns 0

args.name: slot_name
args.description: Slot name as used by /replaceitem, e.g. 'slot.weapon.mainhand'
args.onInvalid: unknown name: content-log error, returns 0; not a string: content-log error

args.name: slot_index
args.description: Slot number inside hotbar, inventory, enderchest or chest
accepts: number; fractional part dropped (truncated toward zero)
required for slot.hotbar, slot.inventory, slot.enderchest, slot.chest
ignored (never evaluated) for all other slots
args.onInvalid: missing where required, or not a number: content-log error, returns 0

appliesTo.entities: any entity with the named slot

whenUnavailable.when: slot name is not a string
index missing for a slot that needs one, or not a number
index out of range, or slot empty

pitfalls: `q.is_cooldown_category('', 'slot.weapon.mainhand')` is 1 for any held item without a category (a sword, a block), not for an empty hand.
`slot.hotbar` without the index is an error, not "the selected slot" - use `slot.weapon.mainhand` for that.
`slot.equippable` read 0 on a horse wearing armor, with or without an index; use `slot.armor.body` for horse armor.
A non-string slot argument returns an empty string rather than 0.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_crawling
queries.summary: Whether the player is crawling (squeezed into a one-block-high space)
queries.hover:
1 while the player is in the crawling pose (pushed into a space one block high), else 0.
Updated by the player's movement each tick; mobs read 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the player is crawling - forced into the low pose because the space is only one block high - otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is crawling and `0` otherwise.

Crawling is the low pose a player takes when there is no room to stand or crouch, for example under a closed trapdoor. The player's movement update switches the flag on and off every tick as the pose changes. Swimming is a separate state with its own query.

Mobs have no crawling pose and read `0` (a zombie pushed into a one-block gap stays at `0`).

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: players; others 0

pitfalls: Swimming and crawling are separate flags; vanilla animations test `q.is_swimming || q.is_crawling`.

queries.name: is_critical
queries.summary: Whether a projectile was fired as a critical shot
queries.hover:
1 while the projectile carries the critical-shot mark, else 0.
Set on arrows from a fully drawn bow and on crossbow arrows; cleared when the projectile hits something.
Other entities never set it; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity - in practice a projectile - is marked as a critical shot, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is marked as a critical shot and `0` otherwise. The mark belongs to projectiles; no mob or player ever receives it.

**When the mark is set.**

| source | condition |
|---|---|
| arrow shot from a bow | the bow was fully drawn (draw power exactly 1) |
| arrow shot from a crossbow | set when the crossbow fires an arrow |
| projectile thrown by an item with `minecraft:projectile` | the throw power reached the item's minimum critical power; a negative minimum disables it |

**When it is cleared.** When the projectile hits and sticks into a block, the mark is removed, so an arrow lying in the ground reads `0` even if it was a critical shot. Flying through water does not clear it; only the impact does. An arrow created by `/summon` never has the mark.

The mark is part of the entity's synchronised state, so resource-pack and behavior-pack Molang see the same value. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: projectiles (arrows, data-driven projectiles); every other entity always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: An arrow that has landed and stuck in a block reads 0 even if it was fired as a critical shot.
A bow drawn to anything less than full power never produces a critical arrow.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_croaking
queries.summary: Whether the entity is running its croak behavior
queries.hover:
1 while the entity's croak behavior is running (the frog's throat-sac animation), else 0.
Only entities with minecraft:behavior.croak ever set it; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is performing its croak behavior, as frogs do, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` for the duration of the entity's croak behavior (`minecraft:behavior.croak`) and `0` otherwise. The behavior turns the flag on when it starts and off when it stops, so the value covers exactly the time the behavior is active.

The behavior runs on the server; the flag is synchronised to clients, so the resource pack sees the same value, typically to drive the croak animation. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:behavior.croak (frogs); others always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_dancing
queries.summary: Whether the entity is dancing to a nearby jukebox
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is dancing to music from a jukebox, else 0.
Only parrots and allays can dance (built in); the dance starts when a record starts playing nearby.
Custom entities always read 0; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is dancing because a jukebox is playing nearby, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is dancing and `0` otherwise.

Dancing is built into the parrot and the allay; there is no JSON component that grants it, so custom entities never dance. The dance starts when a jukebox within the entity's listening distance **starts** playing a record: a parrot or allay brought next to a jukebox that is already playing reads `0` until the record is restarted. The distance is checked again later and the dance ends out of range, but not at once - on the client a dancing parrot teleported 64 blocks away still read `1` four seconds later.

Resource-pack Molang sees both the parrot and the allay dance. For the parrot the dance is set up on the client side, so whether behavior-pack Molang sees a dancing parrot is not yet verified in game. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: parrots and allays only (built in); every other entity always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: A parrot or allay that arrives after the record started does not dance until the record is restarted.
Leaving the listening range ends the dance only after a delay, not on the next tick.
There is no component that makes a custom entity dance; it always reads 0.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_delayed_attacking
queries.summary: Whether a delayed-attack behavior is in its wind-up
queries.hover:
1 from the moment a delayed attack starts until it lands or is cancelled, else 0.
Only entities with minecraft:behavior.delayed_attack set it (the ravager); 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity's delayed-attack behavior has started an attack that has not yet hit or been abandoned, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while an attack from the entity's `minecraft:behavior.delayed_attack` is under way and `0` otherwise.

A delayed attack has a wind-up: the behavior begins the attack, waits, and only then deals the hit. The flag is switched on when the wind-up begins and switched off when the hit is attempted, when the behavior stops (target lost, behavior interrupted) and on its own tick when the attack is abandoned. Use it to play the wind-up animation in step with the damage. A ravager biting a player reads `1` for about 0.6-0.75 seconds of every attack cycle (about 1.5 seconds).

The flag is synchronised to clients. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:behavior.delayed_attack (ravagers); others always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: Other melee behaviors (`behavior.melee_attack`, `behavior.melee_box_attack`) never set it.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_digging
queries.summary: Whether the entity is digging (warden burrowing, sniffer digging)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is digging, else 0.
Set by minecraft:behavior.dig (warden sinking into the ground) and minecraft:behavior.random_search_and_dig (sniffer). 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is digging - the warden burrowing back into the ground or the sniffer digging up a seed - otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is digging and `0` otherwise. Two behaviors set the flag:

| behavior | used by | flag on | flag off |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minecraft:behavior.dig` | warden | when the behavior starts | not switched off by the behavior |
| `minecraft:behavior.random_search_and_dig` | sniffer | when it reaches its spot and starts digging | when digging finishes or the behavior stops |

The dig behavior never clears the flag itself; the warden normally despawns when its dig ends, so in practice the flag stays `1` until the entity is gone.

The flag is synchronised to clients. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:behavior.dig or minecraft:behavior.random_search_and_dig; others always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

queries.name: is_eating
queries.summary: Whether the entity is eating a held or snacked item
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is eating, else 0.
Set by the snacking and eat-carried-item behaviors (pandas, foxes); a grazing sheep reads 0.
0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is eating food it picked up or is holding, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is eating and `0` otherwise.

The flag is set and cleared by two behaviors: `minecraft:behavior.snacking` (a panda eating from its paws) and `minecraft:behavior.eat_carried_item` (eating the item in the entity's mouth or hands, as a fox does). Each turns the flag on while the eating lasts and off when it stops. The value is saved with the entity.

Eating a block, such as a sheep grazing on grass, uses a different mechanism and does not set this flag - use `query.is_grazing` for that. Eating a mob (the frog) is `query.is_eating_mob`.

The flag is synchronised to clients. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:behavior.snacking or minecraft:behavior.eat_carried_item; others always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: A grazing sheep reads 0 here; use `query.is_grazing` for grazing.

1 for elder guardians (and the elder guardian apparition), else 0.
Only the game's guardian code sets it; custom entities cannot. 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity is flagged as the elder form of the guardian, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` for an elder guardian and `0` for everything else.

The flag is set by the guardian's own code: when an elder guardian is created (spawned, summoned or placed by an ocean monument), when a saved elder guardian is loaded, and for the elder guardian apparition shown with the Mining Fatigue effect. There is no component that sets it, so custom entities always read `0`.

The vanilla guardian render controller uses it to pick the elder texture. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

queries.name: is_emerging
queries.summary: Whether the entity is climbing out of the ground (warden emerge)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity's emerge behavior is running, else 0.
Only minecraft:behavior.emerge sets it (the warden rising after being summoned); 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is emerging from the ground through its emerge behavior, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` for as long as the entity's `minecraft:behavior.emerge` runs and `0` otherwise. The behavior sets the flag when it starts and clears it when it stops. The warden, for example, is immune to damage while the flag is on.

queries.name: is_emoting
queries.summary: Whether a player is playing an emote
queries.hover:
1 while the player is playing an emote, else 0.
Players only; moving ends the emote and clears it. 0 for other entities and without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the player is performing an emote, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while a player is performing an emote and `0` otherwise.

Only players have emotes. The flag is switched on when an emote starts and stays on for the emote's length, counted down once per tick; it is cleared when the countdown runs out, or earlier when the player moves enough to interrupt the emote. The value is synchronised, so other players' clients see it too.

It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

queries.name: is_enchanted
queries.summary: Whether a thrown item entity shows the enchantment glint
queries.hover:
1 for projectiles thrown from an item that shows the enchantment glint, else 0.
Set on thrown tridents, splash and lingering potions and bottles o' enchanting; mobs never have it.
0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity is a thrown item that carries the enchantment glint of the item it came from, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the entity was created from an item that shows the enchantment glint, and `0` otherwise. It is about the glint effect, not about enchantments on a mob's equipment.

The flag is set when the projectile is created:

| projectile | set when |
|---|---|
| thrown trident | the trident item shows the glint (it is enchanted) |
| splash potion, lingering potion | the potion item shows the glint |
| bottle o' enchanting | the bottle shows the glint |

The item test is the one that decides whether the item shimmers: an enchanted trident and a bottle o' enchanting read `1` in flight, a plain trident reads `0`; which potions pass it is not yet verified in game. A trident keeps the flag while stuck in the ground and while flying back to a Loyalty owner, and is expected to keep it when the world is saved and loaded (not yet verified). Mobs, players and other entities never receive it.

The flag is synchronised to clients, where it is meant for choosing a glint material. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: thrown tridents, splash/lingering potions, bottles o' enchanting; others always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: Holding or wearing enchanted items does not make a mob `is_enchanted` (a zombie holding an enchanted sword reads 0).

queries.name: is_feeling_happy
queries.summary: Old name for timer_flag_2 (deprecated; only below 1.20.50)
queries.hover:
Deprecated alias: reads the same entity flag as query.timer_flag_2, so the two always agree (0 or 1).
Only resolves in files whose Molang version is below 1.20.50; newer files cannot use the name.
queries.description: Deprecated alias of `query.timer_flag_2`: both names read the same entity flag and give the same 0/1 value.
queries.long:
Gives the same answer as `query.timer_flag_2` in every case, because both names look up one and the same entity flag. See `query.timer_flag_2` for when that flag is on.

**Deprecated.** The name is only recognised in files whose Molang version is older than 1.20.50; in newer files it does not resolve at all: the expression fails to parse and the content log reports that the query cannot be resolved. Use `query.timer_flag_2`.

It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: same entities as query.timer_flag_2 (minecraft:behavior.timer_flag_2); others always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

queries.name: is_fire_immune
queries.summary: Whether the entity is flagged as immune to fire
queries.hover:
1 when the entity is flagged fire-immune, else 0.
Set by minecraft:fire_immune, some damage sensors, area effect clouds and the Fire Resistance effect.
0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity carries the fire-immune flag (from its definition, a lingering cloud or an effect), otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the entity carries the fire-immune flag and `0` otherwise.

**Where the flag comes from.**

| source | effect on the flag |
|---|---|
| `minecraft:fire_immune` component | on while the component is present |
| `minecraft:damage_sensor` with a trigger that marks the entity fire-proof (which trigger settings do this is not yet verified) | on while the component is present |
| area effect clouds (lingering potion clouds) | always on |
| a TNT minecart with a lit fuse | switched on when the fuse is lit, depending on a game rule |
| Fire Resistance effect | switched on when the effect is added and off when it is removed; an entity that is fire-immune by definition (a blaze) stays `1` after the effect is removed |

The flag describes the entity's definition and state, not the damage calculation itself, and it is what path finding and burning-in-daylight checks consult. It is synchronised, so both packs see the same value.

It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

timing.updates: on change of components or effects

pitfalls: The Fire Resistance effect turns the flag on for any mob or player, so the query cannot tell a naturally fire-proof mob from one under the effect.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_first_person
queries.summary: Whether the entity is being drawn in the first-person view
queries.hover:
1 while the client draws the entity (or attachable) as part of the first-person view, else 0.
Resource packs only: behavior packs, particles and blocks get the default 0 (not yet verified in game).
Works without an entity; it reads a value the renderer supplies.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the client is drawing the entity or attachable for the first-person view, otherwise 0. Only meaningful in client entity and attachable files.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the current draw is part of the first-person view and `0` otherwise.

The value is not stored on the entity. It is part of the information the client hands to Molang for each draw, so the same entity can read `1` in one draw and `0` in another (exactly which draws count as first person is not yet verified in game). That makes it usable only in resource-pack files: client entity definitions, render controllers, animations and attachables. Behavior-pack Molang, particles and block expressions are expected to get the default `0` (not yet verified in game).

It does not need an entity, because it only reads the draw information. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored.

Vanilla attachables use the `c.is_first_person` context variable instead of this query; inside an attachable both describe the same thing (not yet verified in game).

appliesTo.entities: any drawn entity or attachable; the value comes from the draw, not the entity

whenUnavailable.when: evaluated outside resource-pack drawing (behavior packs, particles, blocks)

pitfalls: Outside a draw it reads 0 without any log, so a 0 there does not mean third person.
Server-side (behavior-pack) Molang is expected to read 0 (not yet verified in game).
Exactly which draws count as first person (arms, held item, attachables) is not yet verified in game.

1 for the elder guardian apparition shown with Mining Fatigue, else 0.

Returns `1` for the elder guardian apparition - the translucent elder guardian the client flashes on screen when a player receives Mining Fatigue from an elder guardian - and `0` for everything else.

| entity type | result |

| the elder guardian ghost type | always `1` |
| guardian, elder guardian | `1` only for the apparition copy the client creates, otherwise `0` |
| any other entity | always `0` |

Custom entities therefore always read `0`, whatever components they have. The ghost type also reports `query.is_elder` as `1`. The vanilla guardian render controller uses the query to switch to the ghost material. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: guardian types only; everything else always 0

queries.name: is_gliding
queries.summary: Whether a player is gliding with an elytra
queries.hover:
1 while a player is gliding (elytra flight), else 0.
Only players start gliding; a falling mob wearing an elytra reads 0. 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is gliding - a player flying with an elytra - otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the player is in the gliding state and `0` otherwise.

The state starts when a player with an elytra begins to glide (creative players too) and ends when the glide stops, for example on landing. Switching the game mode in mid-glide did not end it in our test. The flag is saved with the player and synchronised, so every client and the behavior pack see it.

Only players have code that starts gliding, so a mob wearing an elytra reads `0` even while falling. It takes no arguments; anything passed in parentheses is ignored. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: players; other entities always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)
