verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_grazing
queries.summary: Whether a sheep or horse-family mob is eating grass
queries.hover:
1 while a sheep or a horse-family mob (horse, donkey, mule, skeleton/zombie horse) is eating grass, else 0.
Any other entity always returns 0, even with an eat-block behavior.
Sheep: 1 for 2 seconds after each eat; horse family: while the head is down (about 2-3 s per bite).
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is in the middle of its grazing animation. Only sheep and the horse family have this state; every other entity returns 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is grazing and `0` otherwise. The query only knows two kinds of grazer, and it answers differently for each:

| entity | what makes it `1` |
|---|---|
| horse family (horse, donkey, mule, skeleton horse, zombie horse) | the mob's own "eating" state, which the server sets while the horse lowers its head to eat and shares with clients (about 2-3 seconds per bite) |
| sheep | a 40-tick (2 second) countdown that restarts each time the sheep's eat-grass event plays; `1` while the countdown is above zero |
| anything else | never - always `0`, including cows, goats, llamas, trader llamas and camels |

Because the list of grazers is fixed, a custom entity with an eat-block behavior still returns `0`; drive such an animation from your own variable or an entity property instead.

For sheep the countdown is started by the eat event that the client receives and runs down on the client, so the query is intended for resource-pack animations. What it returns in behavior-pack Molang for a sheep is not yet verified. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: sheep and horse-family mobs; every other entity always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

timing.updates: per tick (sheep countdown); on change of the flag (horse family)

pitfalls: A custom mob with `minecraft:behavior.eat_block` still returns 0: only sheep and the horse family are recognised.
For sheep the value is a short 2-second window per eat event, not a state that lasts while the goal runs.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_idling
queries.summary: Whether the entity's idling flag is set (few built-in behaviours set it)
queries.hover:
1 if the entity's idling flag is set, else 0.
Only a few built-in behaviours set this flag; ordinary mobs standing still return 0 - it is not a movement test.
0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity carries the idling flag, otherwise 0. Very few behaviours set this flag, so for most mobs it is always 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the entity's idling flag is set and `0` otherwise.

Despite the name, this is **not** a test for "standing still". The flag is written by only a handful of built-in behaviours - a hover-in-place movement behavior and the classroom agent entity; standing still never sets it. For a normal mob that stops walking the query stays `0`; to detect a mob at rest, compare `query.ground_speed` or `query.modified_move_speed` with a small threshold instead.

The flag is part of the entity's synchronised state, so behavior packs and resource packs see the same value. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: It does not mean "not moving": an ordinary mob standing still returns 0.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_ignited
queries.summary: Whether the entity is primed to explode (lit fuse or minecraft:is_ignited)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is flagged as ignited - a lit explosion fuse, or the minecraft:is_ignited component - else 0.
Not about fire: a burning mob is not ignited (use q.is_on_fire).
Entities with minecraft:explode have it rewritten from the fuse state every tick.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is marked as ignited, which happens when its explosion fuse is lit or when it has the `minecraft:is_ignited` component. It has nothing to do with being on fire.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is ignited and `0` otherwise. "Ignited" means *primed to explode*, not burning:

- **Explosion fuse.** For an entity with `minecraft:explode`, the flag is copied from the component's fuse state every tick. A creeper that starts swelling, or any entity whose explode component has `fuse_lit: true`, reads `1` until the fuse is put out or the entity explodes; `query.swell_amount` rises alongside it.
- **`minecraft:is_ignited` component.** Adding the component (for example from a component group) sets the flag; removing the component clears it. On an entity that also has `minecraft:explode`, the fuse state wins on the next tick.

The flag is synchronised, so the value is the same in behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang. A mob that is on fire is not ignited - use `query.is_on_fire` for that. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

timing.updates: per tick for entities with minecraft:explode; otherwise on change of the flag

pitfalls: It is not the burning state: a mob in fire or lava is not ignited.
With `minecraft:explode` present, adding or removing `minecraft:is_ignited` is overridden by the fuse state on the next tick.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_illager_captain
queries.summary: Whether the entity is flagged as an illager captain
queries.hover:
1 if the entity carries the illager-captain flag (the minecraft:is_illager_captain component), else 0.
The flag is saved with the entity and is not tied to wearing the banner.
0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity has the illager-captain flag, which the `minecraft:is_illager_captain` component sets. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the entity carries the illager-captain flag and `0` otherwise.

The flag is set by the `minecraft:is_illager_captain` component - vanilla pillagers and vindicators add it through the component group used for patrol and raid captains - and cleared when the component is removed. It is also stored with the entity, so a captain stays a captain after the world is reloaded.

The query reads the flag only. It does not look at the entity's equipment, so a captain that lost its banner still returns `1`, and a pillager given a banner by other means returns `0`. Any entity type can carry the component. The value is synchronised to clients. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity (vanilla: pillager, vindicator)

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: It does not check for the banner: equipment changes do not affect it.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_in_contact_with_water
queries.summary: Whether the entity is in water or rain, or was just splashed with water
queries.hover:
1 if the entity is in water, is standing in rain, or was splashed by a water bottle this tick, else 0.
The splash part lasts about one tick and is expected only on the server (not yet verified).
Rain counts only where it actually rains (not in snowy biomes or deserts, not under cover, not during the fade-in).
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity is in water or rain (the same test as `query.is_in_water_or_rain`) or was just hit by a splash water bottle. Otherwise 0.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: The splash-bottle case lasts about one tick; do not expect it to hold long enough to drive an animation.
Rain only counts where it rains: snowy biomes and covered spots return 0 during a storm.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_in_lava
queries.summary: Whether the entity is touching lava
queries.hover:
1 while the entity's hitbox is in lava, else 0.
Updated once per tick by the movement code, on both sides; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is in lava, otherwise 0. The state is refreshed once per tick while the entity moves.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is in lava and `0` otherwise.

The game decides this once per tick, as part of the same liquid check that finds water, by testing the blocks the entity's hitbox overlaps; the query just reads the stored result. Both the server and each client run the check, so the query works in behavior packs and resource packs. The hitbox is shrunk by about 0.1 block on each side before the test: a player whose hitbox reached 0.09 block into a lava block read `0`, at 0.115 block `1`. Standing on the edge of a lava pool with the feet just above the lava surface reads `0`.

It is independent of burning: a fire-immune mob wading in lava still reads `1`, and a mob that is still on fire after leaving the lava reads `0`. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: It is not the burning state; use `query.is_on_fire` for that.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_in_love
queries.summary: Whether the entity is in love mode (ready to breed)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is in love mode after being fed its breeding item, else 0.
Cleared when it breeds or when the love period runs out; needs minecraft:breedable to ever be 1.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is in love mode - after it was fed a breeding item and until it breeds or the love period ends. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is in love mode and `0` otherwise.

Love mode belongs to the `minecraft:breedable` component: feeding the entity one of its breed items (or anything else that puts it in love) sets the flag, and it is cleared when the entity breeds, when the love timer runs out, or when love is reset. An entity without `minecraft:breedable` never enters love mode and always returns `0`.

The flag is synchronised, so the same value is seen in behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang - handy for a custom heart particle or an animation. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:breedable; others always 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_in_ui
queries.summary: Whether the entity is being drawn as a preview inside a UI screen
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is rendered as a user-interface preview (e.g. the player model in the inventory), else 0.
Meant for resource packs; behavior-pack Molang is not expected to see it set (not yet verified).
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity is being drawn as a preview inside a screen, such as the player model in the inventory, rather than in the world. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is being rendered as part of a user-interface screen - the player preview in the inventory, the dressing room and similar model previews - and `0` when it is drawn in the world.

It is meant for render controllers and client animations that should look different in a preview, for example hiding a base plate or skipping a world-only effect. The flag is raised by the client's interface renderer, so behavior-pack Molang does not see it set (not yet verified in game). Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: It says nothing about whether a screen is open: the in-world copy of the player reads 0 while the inventory is open.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; this behaviour cannot be observed from the client in game, so it is not verified there

queries.name: is_in_water
queries.summary: Whether the entity is touching water
queries.hover:
1 while the entity's hitbox is in water, else 0.
Rain does not count (see q.is_in_water_or_rain). Updated once per tick on both sides; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is in water, otherwise 0. Rain does not count.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is in water and `0` otherwise.

The game decides this once per tick, in the same liquid check that finds lava, by testing the blocks the entity's hitbox overlaps; the query only reads the stored result. The check runs on the server and on clients, so behavior packs and resource packs both get it. Standing with only the feet in one block of water counts, a bubble column counts, and so does standing on top of a waterlogged bottom slab (the water in the slab's block is enough, with no free water around).

Being fully under water is a stronger condition than this query - look at `query.is_breathing` or `query.is_swimming` when that is what you need. Rain is never counted here; `query.is_in_water_or_rain` and `query.is_in_contact_with_water` add it. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: Touching water is enough; it does not mean submerged.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_in_water_or_rain
queries.summary: Whether the entity is in water or rain is falling on it
queries.hover:
1 if the entity is in water or rain falls on the block at the top of its hitbox, else 0.
Rain needs open sky, a storm past its fade-in, and a biome where it rains (snow and deserts give 0).
0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity is in water (as `query.is_in_water`) or rain is falling where the top of its hitbox is. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when either of these is true, and `0` otherwise:

- the entity is in water - exactly `query.is_in_water`;
- it is raining **at the block containing the top of the entity's hitbox**: it must be raining, that block must be exposed to the sky, and the biome there must be warm enough for rain rather than snow.

"Raining" means the storm is well under way: while the rain is still fading in or out at the start and end of a storm, the rain part stays `0` - about a second after the weather changes to rain in our test. Biomes where it never rains, such as deserts, give `0` too.

The rain test is made at the entity's horizontal position, at the height of its position plus its hitbox height. For mobs the position is at the feet, so the test point is the top of the hitbox. For players the position is at eye level, so the point is about 3.4 blocks above the feet: a roof directly over a player's head (two blocks above the feet) does not stop the rain part, a roof three blocks up does. Any block at or above the test point stops the rain part; so does a snowy or frozen biome during a storm. The rain part is computed each time the query runs, while the water part is the once-per-tick result.

Without an entity the query returns `0`. To also catch a splash water bottle, use `query.is_in_contact_with_water`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

timing.updates: on read (rain part); per tick (water part)

pitfalls: Snow does not count: in cold biomes a storm gives 0.
Cover anywhere above the test point, such as a roof or a tree canopy, blocks the rain part.
For players the test point is about 3.4 blocks above the feet, so a low ceiling right over the head does not keep them out of the rain.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_interested
queries.summary: Whether the mob is showing interest (wolf begging, fox stalking prey)
queries.hover:
1 while a begging or prey-stalking behavior has marked the mob as interested, else 0.
Set by minecraft:behavior.beg (wolves) and minecraft:behavior.stalk_and_pounce_on_target (foxes); otherwise 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the mob's interested flag is set - by the beg behavior (a wolf tilting its head at food) or while a fox creeps up on prey. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity's interested flag is set and `0` otherwise.

Two behaviors set the flag:

| behavior | when the flag is on |
|---|---|
| `minecraft:behavior.beg` | from the moment the mob starts begging at a player holding one of its items until it stops |
| `minecraft:behavior.stalk_and_pounce_on_target` | while the mob is creeping toward its prey; it is switched off when the mob prepares to pounce and when the behavior ends |

Any entity that uses one of these behaviors gets the flag, not only wolves and foxes. The flag is synchronised to clients, which is how the vanilla head-tilt and wiggle animations use it. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities running minecraft:behavior.beg or minecraft:behavior.stalk_and_pounce_on_target; others 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_invisible
queries.summary: Whether the entity is invisible (normally the Invisibility effect)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is invisible - normally because it has the Invisibility effect - else 0.
Becoming invisible also hides the entity's name tag; the value is synchronised to clients.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is invisible, which normally means it has the Invisibility effect. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is invisible and `0` otherwise.

The flag follows the Invisibility effect: when the effect is gained the flag is switched on, and when it ends or is cleared the flag goes off. A few game systems can also make an entity invisible directly. Whenever the flag changes, the game also switches off (or back on) the entity's ability to show its name tag and plays the matching sound.

The flag is synchronised, so render controllers and behavior packs agree. The query does not look at materials, textures or `query.is_on_screen`; an invisible entity is still "on screen" when it is in view. Vanilla uses it to swap to an invisible-friendly material or hide geometry. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: It is the Invisibility state, not whether the entity is currently visible on screen.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_item_equipped
queries.summary: Whether the main hand or off hand holds any item
queries.hover:
`q.is_item_equipped([hand])` - 1 if that hand holds an item: 0 or 'main_hand' (default), 1 or 'off_hand'.
For players the main hand is the selected hotbar slot. Extra arguments are ignored.
Any other value (2, -1, 'mainhand', '') logs an error and returns 0; fractions are truncated (0.9 = main hand).
queries.description: Returns 1 when the chosen hand holds an item and 0 when it is empty. With no argument it checks the main hand.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the chosen hand holds an item and `0` when it is empty. It does not care which item it is - use `query.is_item_name_any` or `query.equipped_item_any_tag` to test for a specific one.

```
q.is_item_equipped
q.is_item_equipped('off_hand')
```

**Hand.** No argument, `0` or `'main_hand'` checks the main hand; `1` or `'off_hand'` checks the off hand. Numbers have their fractional part dropped, so `0.9` and `-0.5` mean the main hand and `1.5` means the off hand. Anything else - `2`, `'mainhand'`, `'OFF_HAND'`, `''` - writes an error to the content log and returns `0`. Whole negative numbers such as `-1` are rejected the same way on Windows; on ARM devices they may count as the main hand instead, so do not pass them. Only the first argument is read; any further arguments are ignored without a warning.

For players the main hand is the item in the selected hotbar slot; for mobs it is the item they carry in their hand.

Without an entity the query returns `0` without logging, even if the hand argument is invalid.

args.name: hand
args.description: Which hand to check
accepts: numbers truncated toward zero (0.9 -> 0, 1.5 -> 1); -1 and below: error on Windows, may read as main hand on ARM
args.onInvalid: content-log error, returns 0

appliesTo.entities: players and mobs (anything with hands); others read as empty

pitfalls: `'mainhand'` / `'offhand'` (no underscore) are errors; only `'main_hand'` and `'off_hand'` are accepted.
`q.is_item_equipped(-1)` logs an error and returns 0 on Windows, but may check the main hand on ARM devices.
A second argument is ignored, so `q.is_item_equipped(1, 0)` still checks the off hand.

verification.label: Verified in game on 1.26.60.22 (client side)

queries.name: is_item_name_any
queries.summary: Whether the item in an equipment slot matches any of the given identifiers
queries.hover:
`q.is_item_name_any(slot, [index], 'ns:item', ...)` - 1 if the item in that slot is any of the listed items.
Slot names are the /replaceitem names ('slot.weapon.mainhand', 'slot.hotbar', ...). Identifiers need the namespace.
'' matches an empty slot - and also a slot or index the entity does not have.
Multi-slot containers (hotbar, inventory, chest, ...) need the index; without it the slot reads as empty.
queries.description: Looks at one equipment or inventory slot of the entity and returns 1 when the item there is one of the listed item identifiers, otherwise 0. An empty string matches an empty slot.
queries.long:
Checks the item in one slot of the entity against a list of item identifiers.

```
q.is_item_name_any(slot_name, 'minecraft:bow', 'minecraft:crossbow')
q.is_item_name_any(slot_name, slot_index, 'minecraft:bow')
```

**Slot name.** One of the names used by `/replaceitem`: `slot.weapon.mainhand`, `slot.weapon.offhand`, `slot.armor.head`, `slot.armor.chest`, `slot.armor.legs`, `slot.armor.feet`, `slot.armor.body`, `slot.hotbar`, `slot.inventory`, `slot.enderchest`, `slot.saddle`, `slot.armor`, `slot.chest`, `slot.equippable`. Any other string logs an error and returns 0.

**Slot index.** If the second argument is a number, it picks the slot inside a multi-slot container (`slot.hotbar`, `slot.inventory`, `slot.enderchest`, `slot.chest`, `slot.equippable`); the fractional part is dropped. Hands, armor, saddle and horse armor ignore it. If the second argument is a string it is the first identifier to compare, and no index is used.

**Identifiers.** Compared exactly as written, including the namespace: `'minecraft:bow'` matches, `'bow'` does not. The empty string `''` matches when the slot holds nothing.

**Which entities have which slots.**

| slot | who has it |
|---|---|
| `slot.weapon.mainhand` | players (the selected hotbar slot) and mobs |
| `slot.weapon.offhand` | players and mobs |
| `slot.armor.head/chest/legs/feet/body` | mobs (players included) |
| `slot.hotbar`, `slot.enderchest` | players |
| `slot.inventory` | players, and entities with an inventory |
| `slot.saddle`, `slot.armor` | horse-like entities |
| `slot.chest` | entities currently carrying a chest |
| `slot.equippable` | mobs with an equipment container |

A slot the entity does not have, an index outside the container, or a missing index for a multi-slot container all behave like an empty slot: `''` matches and every identifier fails.

In resource-pack Molang the client does not know what is in the saddle, chest and ender chest slots: they read as empty. Horse armor is visible there through `slot.armor.body`, while `slot.armor` reads empty.

Prefer this query to `query.get_equipped_item_name`: it takes full identifiers, works for any slot, and does not force you to compare strings yourself.

args.name: slot_name
args.description: Equipment slot name as used by /replaceitem
args.onInvalid: content-log error, returns 0

args.name: slot_index
args.description: Index inside a multi-slot container; only recognised when it is a number
accepts: number; truncated toward zero (-0.5 reads slot 0)
negative indices read as an empty slot
omitted: the second argument is treated as the first identifier
args.onInvalid: out-of-range index: slot reads as empty, no log

args.name: item
args.description: Full item identifier with namespace, or '' for an empty slot
args.onInvalid: a non-string reached during matching: content-log error, returns 0

appliesTo.entities: any entity; each slot exists only on some entity types (see table)

whenUnavailable.when: second argument neither number nor string
slot or index the entity does not have
exactly two arguments and the second is a number (no identifiers)

pitfalls: Omitting the index on `slot.hotbar` (or another multi-slot container) makes the slot read as empty - `''` then matches.
Identifiers without a namespace never match, and the comparison is case-sensitive.
In resource packs use `slot.armor.body` for horse armor; `slot.armor`, `slot.saddle`, `slot.chest` and `slot.enderchest` read as empty on the client.
Arguments are checked lazily: a wrong argument after the first match is never reported.
`q.is_item_name_any('slot.hotbar', 0)` (index but no identifiers) is always 0 and logs nothing.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_jump_goal_jumping
queries.summary: Whether a jump behavior (jump to block, jump around target) is mid-jump
queries.hover:
1 while a jump behavior has the mob in a jump, else 0.
Set by minecraft:behavior.jump_to_block and minecraft:behavior.jump_around_target only; a normal jump is 0 (use q.is_jumping).
queries.description: Returns 1 while one of the jump behaviors - jump to block or jump around target - has the mob in the middle of a jump. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while a jump performed by a jump behavior is in progress and `0` otherwise.

| behavior | flag on | flag off |
|---|---|---|
| `minecraft:behavior.jump_to_block` (frog, goat) | when the mob leaves the ground toward the chosen block | when the jump finishes or the behavior is reset |
| `minecraft:behavior.jump_around_target` (breeze) | when the behavior starts its jump | when the behavior stops |

Ordinary jumps - a mob hopping up a block while walking, or a player pressing jump - do not set this flag; `query.is_jumping` covers those. The flag is synchronised, so animation controllers can switch on it. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities running a jump behavior; others 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: A normal jump is not a jump-goal jump; use `query.is_jumping` for those.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_jumping
queries.summary: Whether the entity is in the jumping state of its movement
queries.hover:
1 while the entity's movement is in its jumping state, else 0.
Players: 1 the whole time jump is held and they are not flying, even on the ground. Mobs: jump control (server).
Not the same as being airborne; combine with q.is_on_ground for that.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity's movement code has it in the jumping state, otherwise 0. For players this follows the jump input; for mobs, their jump control.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is in its jumping state and `0` otherwise. The state is kept by the movement code and refreshed every tick:

- **Players** enter it while the jump input is active and they are not flying; flying (for example in creative) turns it off.
- **Mobs** enter it when their movement asks for a jump (climbing a step, jumping out of water, a jump attack) and leave it when the jump ends.

It is not a test for being in the air: a falling player or mob that never jumped reads `0`, and a player holding jump reads `1` for the whole time the key is held - between hops and even under a ceiling that stops the jump. The mob side was not seen on the client: a hopping slime read `0` in resource-pack Molang. Use `!query.is_on_ground` for "airborne", and `query.is_jump_goal_jumping` for jumps made by jump behaviors.

Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: Falling is not jumping: use `!query.is_on_ground` to detect being airborne.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_laying_down
queries.summary: Whether the mob is lying down through the lay-down behavior
queries.hover:
1 while minecraft:behavior.lay_down has the mob lying down, else 0.
Sitting, sleeping and resting are separate states with their own queries; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the mob is lying down because of the lay-down behavior, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity's laying-down flag is set and `0` otherwise.

The flag is switched on when `minecraft:behavior.lay_down` starts and off when it stops, and it is saved with the entity, so a mob that was lying down when the world was saved is still lying down after loading. Nothing else turns it on: a sitting pet, a sleeping fox or villager and a resting bat are reported by `query.is_sitting`, `query.is_sleeping` and `query.is_resting` instead.

The flag is synchronised to clients. Without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities running minecraft:behavior.lay_down; others 0

whenUnavailable.when: no entity in the context (world particles, blocks)

pitfalls: Sitting or sleeping mobs return 0; each of those states has its own query.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_laying_egg
queries.summary: Whether the mob is currently digging in to lay eggs (turtles, frogs)
queries.hover:
1 while the mob's lay-egg behaviour is in its laying phase, else 0.
Any mob with that behaviour (vanilla: turtle and frog); switches back to 0 as soon as the egg is placed.
Synced flag, so resource and behavior packs agree; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the mob is in the egg-laying phase of its lay-egg behaviour, otherwise 0. Vanilla turtles and frogs use that behaviour.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while a mob is laying eggs and `0` otherwise.

The value is switched on by the lay-egg AI behaviour when the mob has reached its spot and starts laying, and switched off in the same tick the egg block (turtle eggs, frogspawn) is placed. It is not tied to the turtle: any entity whose behavior file uses the lay-egg behaviour sets it, which in vanilla means turtles and frogs. A mob that is merely carrying eggs (pregnant) reads `0` until it actually starts laying.

The value is part of the entity's synchronised flags, so behavior-pack and resource-pack expressions see the same state. It takes no arguments; anything passed in brackets is ignored and never evaluated. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: mobs with the lay-egg behaviour; all others always 0

examples.expr: query.is_laying_egg ? math.cos(query.life_time * 1146.0) * 90.0 : math.clamp(math.cos(query.anim_time * variable.timemultiplier * variable.legspeedmultiplier * 57.3) * variable.frontlegmultiplier * query.modified_move_speed * 57.3, -90.0, 90.0) - this

pitfalls: Carrying eggs is not laying them: use `query.is_pregnant` for the time between breeding and reaching the nest.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; not yet verified in game

queries.name: is_leashed
queries.summary: Whether the entity is on a lead
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is attached to a lead (held by a player, tied to a fence post or another mob), else 0.
Synced flag - resource and behavior packs agree; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is attached to a lead, whatever holds the other end, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while a lead is attached to the entity and `0` otherwise.

It does not matter what holds the other end: a player, a fence knot or another mob all count. The flag is set when the lead is attached, cleared when the lead breaks or is removed, restored from the save when the entity is loaded, and synchronised to clients. It takes no arguments; anything passed in brackets is ignored and never evaluated. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity that can be leashed

pitfalls: It is 1 for a mob tied to a fence as well - it does not mean a player is leading it.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_levitating
queries.summary: Whether the entity has the Levitation effect
queries.hover:
1 while the entity has the Levitation effect (any level, any remaining time), else 0.
Checks the effect only - being pushed upward by anything else does not count. 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the Levitation status effect is active on the entity, at any level, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity has the Levitation effect and `0` otherwise.

Only the presence of the effect is checked: its level and remaining duration do not matter, and an effect that has been hidden (no particles) still counts. Upward motion from other sources - bubble columns, wind charges, flying - is not levitation.

Anything that accepts effects counts, armor stands included. Effects are sent to clients, so resource-pack animations see the effect once it arrives (the server side itself was not measured). It takes no arguments; anything passed in brackets is ignored and never evaluated. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities that can carry status effects; others always 0

pitfalls: It tells you nothing about vertical speed: a levitating mob stuck under a ceiling still reads 1.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_lingering
queries.summary: Whether a thrown potion is a lingering potion
queries.hover:
1 for a thrown lingering potion in flight (thrown by hand or shot from a dispenser), else 0.
Splash potions and the effect cloud a lingering potion leaves behind read 0. 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 for a thrown potion entity that came from a lingering potion, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the entity is a thrown lingering potion and `0` for everything else.

Only the thrown-potion projectile gets this flag, at the moment it is created from a lingering potion - thrown by a player or fired by a dispenser. A splash potion reads `0`, and so does the area-effect cloud that appears where a lingering potion lands (the cloud is a separate entity). It is useful in the thrown potion's own client entity to tell the two potion kinds apart. It takes no arguments; anything passed in brackets is ignored and never evaluated. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: thrown potions; every other entity 0

pitfalls: Testing it on the area-effect cloud gives 0 - the flag lives on the projectile, not on the cloud.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_local_player
queries.summary: Whether the entity is a player controlled on this client
queries.hover:
1 if the entity is a player controlled by this game instance, else 0. Resource packs only.
Evaluated on the server (behavior packs) it returns 0 and writes a content-log error every time.
Without an entity: 0 plus a content-log error.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity is a player that is controlled on this client (the person at this screen), and 0 for every other entity, including other players. Meant for resource packs.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the entity is a player controlled by this game instance and `0` for all other entities, including the other players you see in multiplayer. Typical use is to render something differently for your own player.

**Where it works.** Only in client-side (resource-pack) expressions. When it is evaluated on the server - behavior-pack Molang - it returns `0` and writes an error to the content log on every evaluation, so keep it out of behavior files and animation controllers that run server-side.

**Split-screen.** Each local player is controlled by this instance, so each of them should read `1` in every view, not only in its own; this is not yet verified.

It takes no arguments. Without an entity it returns `0` and writes a content-log error.

appliesTo.entities: players controlled on this client; everything else 0

whenUnavailable.when: entity is not a locally controlled player

pitfalls: In a behavior pack it does not just return 0 - it fills the content log with an error each time.
Other players in multiplayer are 0; it is not the same as testing for the player type.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_moving
queries.summary: Whether the entity changed position noticeably during the last tick
queries.hover:
1 if the entity moved more than about 0.03 blocks in the last tick (about 0.6 blocks/s), else 0.
Vertical movement counts. Players: held movement input decides, not position. Per tick.
Synced flag; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity moved more than a small threshold (about 0.03 blocks) during the last tick, otherwise 0. For players it reflects held movement input instead.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is moving and `0` when it is (almost) still.

**How it is decided.** Once per tick the game compares the entity's position with its position one tick earlier. If the squared distance is above `0.001` - a move of more than about **0.032 blocks in one tick**, roughly **0.63 blocks per second** - the flag is set, otherwise cleared. All three directions count, so a mob that is rising under Levitation reads `1` even when it is not walking.

**Players.** For the player on this client the movement input decides: it is `1` while the movement keys or stick are held - also when walking into a wall, and also while steering a boat - and `0` when the player is moved without input, for example pushed by a piston.

**AI movement.** The movement controllers of walking, swimming and dolphin-like mobs also switch it on while they are driving the mob towards a target.

The flag is synchronised from the server. On a client a mob's value can be a tick or two out of step with the smoothed position you see, so at the very start or end of a movement it can disagree with `query.ground_speed`. It takes no arguments; anything passed in brackets is ignored and never evaluated. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity whose movement is simulated; players by input

pitfalls: Falling or being pushed counts as moving - combine with `query.is_on_ground` for a walk animation.
Very slow movement (under about 0.6 blocks per second) reads 0.
A player pressing forward against a wall reads 1; a player pushed by a piston without input reads 0.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_name_any
queries.summary: Whether the entity's name tag equals any of the given strings
queries.hover:
`q.is_name_any('name', ...)` - 1 if the entity's name tag (custom name, player name) equals any argument.
Exact, case-sensitive match on the displayed name, not the entity type.
Stops at the first match; no arguments, no entity or a non-string argument log an error and give 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 if the entity's name tag - the custom name given with a name tag, or a player's name - is exactly equal to one of the string arguments, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Compares the entity's name tag with each argument in turn and returns `1` on the first exact match.

The name tag is the custom name shown above the entity: a name given with a name tag item, a name set by command or script, or a player's name. It is not the entity type - use `query.is_owner_identifier_any` or the type itself for that. The comparison is on the exact text: case, spaces and formatting codes all matter.

An entity without a custom name has an empty name, so `q.is_name_any('')` is `1` for unnamed entities and `0` for named ones.

**Arguments.** One or more strings. Arguments are checked from left to right and evaluation stops at the first match, so a bad argument after the matching one is never looked at. Reaching an argument that is not a string writes an error naming its position (counted from 0) and returns `0`. No arguments at all, or no entity, also log an error and return `0`.

args.name: name
args.description: Name to compare with; repeat for more
args.onInvalid: not a string: content-log error naming its position (from 0), returns 0 - only if no earlier argument matched

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: an argument reached before any match is not a string

pitfalls: It matches the display name, not the entity type: q.is_name_any('minecraft:pig') is 0 for a pig.
'Steve' and 'steve' are different names.
A typo after the matching argument goes unnoticed because later arguments are not checked.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_on_fire
queries.summary: Whether the entity is burning (with per-type exceptions)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is burning, else 0.
Exceptions: a blaze reads 1 only while charged to attack; magma cubes, shulker bullets and wither skulls are always 0.
Resource and behavior packs agree; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is burning, otherwise 0. A few entity types answer differently: blazes report their charged (attacking) state, and magma cubes, shulker bullets and wither skulls always report 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is on fire and `0` otherwise.

For most entities this follows the burning state: it becomes `1` when the entity catches fire (fire, lava, fire aspect, flaming arrows, sunlight for undead) and returns to `0` when the fire goes out or is extinguished. The server keeps the burn timer and clients follow the synchronised burning flag, so both sides agree.

Some entity types replace the answer:

| entity | value |
|---|---|
| blaze | `1` only while charged (glowing, about to shoot), regardless of real burning |
| magma cube, shulker bullet, wither skull | always `0` |
| everything else | burning state |

`query.is_onfire` reads the synchronised burning flag directly and skips these exceptions, so for the four types above the two spellings can disagree. It takes no arguments; anything passed in brackets is ignored and never evaluated. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity; blaze, magma cube, shulker bullet and wither skull answer differently

pitfalls: On a blaze this is its attack-charge state, not whether it is burning.
Not an alias of `query.is_onfire` - the two differ for blazes, magma cubes, shulker bullets and wither skulls.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_on_ground
queries.summary: Whether the entity is standing on a block
queries.hover:
1 while the entity rests on the ground after the last movement step, else 0 (jumping, falling).
Changes once per tick, not smoothed; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity's last movement step ended resting on a block, otherwise 0 - for example while jumping, falling, flying or floating in water.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the entity is standing on something and `0` when it is in the air or floating.

The value is the ground contact recorded by the entity's latest movement step, expected to be set when downward movement was stopped by something solid and cleared otherwise. It changes once per tick and is not smoothed between frames. In water it is `1` only while the entity rests on the bottom.

For other players and remote entities a client uses the ground contact received with their movement updates, so it can lag the server by the network delay. It takes no arguments; anything passed in brackets is ignored and never evaluated. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

pitfalls: In water a swimming mob reads 0 until it rests on the bottom - pair it with `query.is_in_water`.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_on_screen
queries.summary: Whether the entity was inside the camera view in the latest frame
queries.hover:
1 if the entity was inside the camera's view in the most recent rendered frame, else 0.
Set by the client while drawing; server-side Molang can be expected to read 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity was within the camera's view the last time the client drew a frame, and 0 when it was culled (behind the camera or outside the view).
queries.long:
Each frame the client decides which entities fall inside the camera's view and records the result on the entity. This query returns that record: `1` for an entity that was in view in the latest frame, `0` for one that was culled.

Being "in view" is a frustum test, not a line-of-sight test: an entity hidden behind a wall is still on screen.

Only the client's renderer sets the flag, so the value is only meaningful in resource-pack Molang. Entities drawn by the few remaining built-in renderers do not update it. Without an entity the query returns `0`. It takes no arguments.

While an entity is off screen, its other per-frame values (such as `query.life_time`) are not refreshed either; they hold their last drawn value until the entity is back in view.

appliesTo.entities: entities drawn with data-driven render controllers

pitfalls: It is a view-frustum test: walls and other blocks between the camera and the entity do not change it.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_onfire
queries.summary: Whether the entity's burning flag is set (no per-type exceptions)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity's synchronised burning flag is set, else 0.
Unlike `query.is_on_fire` there are no per-type exceptions (blaze, magma cube, shulker bullet, wither skull).
0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity's burning flag is set, otherwise 0. Reads the flag directly, without the per-type exceptions of query.is_on_fire.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity's burning flag is set and `0` otherwise.

The server sets the flag while the entity's burn timer runs and clears it when the fire stops; clients receive it with the other entity flags. For most entities this is exactly what `query.is_on_fire` returns.

The difference: `query.is_on_fire` lets some entity types answer for themselves (a blaze reports its charged state; magma cubes, shulker bullets and wither skulls report `0`). This spelling does not, so on those types it shows the real burning flag. It takes no arguments; anything passed in brackets is ignored and never evaluated. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

pitfalls: For a blaze this and `query.is_on_fire` answer different questions.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_orphaned
queries.summary: Whether a tamed mob's owner no longer exists in this world
queries.hover:
1 for a tamed mob that was loaded while its owner has no player data in the world, else 0.
Checked when the mob's chunk loads; cleared when a player interacts with it to make it sit.
0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 for a tamed mob whose owner could not be found among the world's players when the mob was loaded, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` for a tamed animal that has lost its owner, and `0` otherwise.

**When it is set.** When a chunk loads, every tamed mob in it is checked: if no player saved in this world has the owner's id - the owner never joined this copy of the world, for example after the world was shared or the player data was removed - the mob is marked orphaned. A mob that is already marked is not checked again; untamed mobs are never marked.

**When it is cleared.** When a player interacts with the mob to make it sit or stand, and when the entity is created. The mark is kept in the save.

The flag is synchronised to clients. It takes no arguments; anything passed in brackets is ignored and never evaluated. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: tamed mobs; others always 0

pitfalls: A tamed mob whose owner is simply offline is not orphaned - only an owner missing from the world's player data counts.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; this behaviour cannot be observed from the client in game, so it is not verified there

queries.name: is_owner_identifier_any
queries.summary: Whether the context entity's type identifier equals any given one
queries.hover:
`q.is_owner_identifier_any('minecraft:player', ...)` - 1 if the entity type matches any argument.
Checks the entity the expression runs for; in an attachable that is expected to be the wearer/holder.
Write the full identifier with namespace. Stops at the first match; errors log and give 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 if the type identifier of the entity the expression is evaluated for equals one of the string arguments, otherwise 0. In attachables this is the entity using the item.
queries.long:
Compares the identifier of the entity in the current context - `minecraft:player`, `minecraft:zombie`, `my_pack:robot` - with each argument and returns `1` on the first match.

**Which entity.** The expression's own entity: for a client entity it is the entity itself; in an attachable it is the entity the item or armour is attached to, which is why the query is used there to pick a model per wearer. No owner chain is followed beyond that - a projectile's shooter or a tamed mob's owner is not consulted. The attachable case is not verified in game.

**The identifier.** The full name with namespace, exactly as declared (`minecraft:pig`). A name without the namespace does not match, and neither does different letter case.

**Arguments.** One or more strings, checked from left to right; evaluation stops at the first match. Reaching an argument that is not a string writes an error naming its position (counted from 0) and returns `0`. No arguments, or no entity, also log an error and return `0`.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Entity identifier with namespace; repeat for more
args.onInvalid: not a string: content-log error naming its position (from 0), returns 0 - only if no earlier argument matched

appliesTo.entities: any entity (attachables: the wearer/holder)

whenUnavailable.when: an argument reached before any match is not a string

pitfalls: Despite the name it does not look up a tamed mob's or projectile's owner.
'player' without 'minecraft:' does not match.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_pack_setting_enabled
queries.summary: Whether a toggle pack setting is switched on
queries.hover:
`q.is_pack_setting_enabled('name')` - 1 if the toggle setting with that name is on, else 0. Resource packs only.
Only toggles: a slider, dropdown or unknown name writes a content-log error and gives 0.
On the server it logs an error; with no settings in any active pack it is silently 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 if the named toggle in the pack settings screen is switched on, otherwise 0. Resource packs only.
queries.long:
Reads a toggle that a resource pack declares for its settings screen and returns `1` when the player has it switched on.

**Argument.** Exactly one string: the setting's name as declared by the pack. The setting must be a toggle. A name that does not exist, or that belongs to a slider, dropdown or multi-select setting, writes an error to the content log and returns `0`. A non-string argument or a different number of arguments also log an error.

**Where it works.** Client-side only. It needs an entity or a level context to find the settings; on the server (behavior packs) it writes an error and returns `0`. If no active pack declares any settings at all, the query quietly returns `0` without checking the name.

The value changes as soon as the player changes the setting. Dropdowns and multi-selects are read with `query.is_pack_setting_selected`, sliders with `query.get_pack_setting`.

args.name: setting
args.description: Name of a toggle setting
args.onInvalid: not a string, unknown name or not a toggle: content-log error, returns 0

appliesTo.entities: any (needs an entity or a level context)

whenUnavailable.when: no entity and no level available
no active pack defines any settings
no setting with that name, or the setting is not a toggle

pitfalls: Using it on a dropdown setting logs an error; use `query.is_pack_setting_selected` there.
In a world with no pack settings at all a misspelt name returns 0 silently instead of logging.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; this behaviour cannot be observed from the client in game, so it is not verified there

queries.name: is_pack_setting_selected
queries.summary: Whether a dropdown or multi-select pack setting has an option chosen
queries.hover:
`q.is_pack_setting_selected('setting', 'option')` - 1 if that option is chosen, else 0. Resource packs only.
Dropdown: the chosen option equals it; multi-select: it is among the chosen ones.
An option name the setting does not have is silently 0; toggles, sliders and unknown settings log an error.
queries.description: Returns 1 if the named dropdown setting has the given option chosen, or the named multi-select setting includes it, otherwise 0. Resource packs only.
queries.long:
Tests one option of a dropdown or multi-select pack setting.

| setting kind | result |
|---|---|
| dropdown | `1` when the chosen option is the one named |
| multi-select | `1` when the named option is among the chosen ones |
| toggle, slider, or no such setting | `0` with a content-log error |

**Arguments.** Exactly two strings: the setting name and the option name, both as declared by the pack. Both are evaluated before they are checked; a non-string in either position logs an error naming that position (0 or 1). The option name is not validated: a misspelt option simply never matches and returns `0` without any log line.

**Where it works.** Client-side only, with an entity or a level context, exactly like `query.is_pack_setting_enabled`: on the server it logs an error and returns `0`, and in a world where no active pack declares settings it returns `0` without checking anything.

args.name: setting
args.description: Name of a dropdown or multi-select setting
args.onInvalid: not a string, unknown, or a toggle/slider: content-log error, returns 0

args.name: option
args.description: Name of the option to test
args.onInvalid: not a string: content-log error; unknown option: 0 without a log

appliesTo.entities: any (needs an entity or a level context)

whenUnavailable.when: no entity and no level available
no active pack defines any settings
either argument is not a string
no setting with that name, or it is a toggle or slider
option name not chosen or not an option of the setting

pitfalls: A typo in the option name is never reported - the query just stays 0.
Toggles are read with `query.is_pack_setting_enabled`; passing a toggle here logs an error.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; this behaviour cannot be observed from the client in game, so it is not verified there

queries.name: is_persona_or_premium_skin
queries.summary: Whether a player wears a character-creator or Marketplace skin
queries.hover:
1 if the entity is a player whose skin is a character-creator skin or a premium (Marketplace) skin, else 0.
Non-player entities are always 0; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity is a player wearing a character-creator skin or a premium skin, otherwise 0. Other entities always return 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` for a player whose current skin is either made in the character creator or a premium skin, and `0` for players with a classic custom or default skin.

Only players have skins: every other entity returns `0`. The value comes from the skin data the player joined with (or changed to), which every client is expected to receive for every player (not yet verified). Being exactly `0` or `1`, it can index a two-entry array directly, which is how vanilla uses it to pick a geometry.

It takes no arguments; arguments passed anyway are ignored. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: players; other entities always 0

timing.updates: on change of the player's skin

pitfalls: It does not say which of the two kinds the skin is.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_playing_dead
queries.summary: Whether the mob is playing dead (axolotl behaviour)
queries.hover:
1 while the mob's play-dead behaviour is running, else 0 (vanilla: axolotls).
Synced flag - resource and behavior packs agree; 0 without an entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the mob's play-dead behaviour is active, otherwise 0. Vanilla axolotls play dead when badly hurt.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while a mob is playing dead and `0` otherwise.

The flag is switched on when the play-dead AI behaviour starts (an axolotl that took damage and is low on health) and off when the behaviour stops. Any entity whose behavior file uses the play-dead behaviour sets it; in vanilla that is only the axolotl. It is also cleared when the entity is created or reloaded. It takes no arguments; anything passed in brackets is ignored and never evaluated. Without an entity it returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: mobs with the play-dead behaviour; others always 0

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_powered
queries.summary: Whether the entity is powered (charged creeper), set by minecraft:is_charged
queries.hover:
1 while the entity has the `minecraft:is_charged` component (a lightning-charged creeper), else 0.
Not the same flag as `query.is_charged`, which blazes and pillagers use.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is powered - the state a creeper gets from a lightning strike - and 0 otherwise. The state comes from the `minecraft:is_charged` component.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is powered and `0` otherwise.

The powered state is switched on when the `minecraft:is_charged` component is added to the entity and switched off when that component is removed. Vanilla creepers get the component (through a component group) when lightning strikes near them, which is why the vanilla charged-creeper overlay tests this query. Any custom entity can use the same component to drive its own "powered" visuals.

Nothing else turns the state on: explosions, redstone power and the creeper's fuse do not affect it.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with the minecraft:is_charged component; others always 0

pitfalls: The names cross over: the `minecraft:is_charged` component drives `query.is_powered`, while `query.is_charged` reads a different state (a blaze's fire attack, a pillager loading its crossbow). A charged creeper reads `q.is_charged == 0`.
It has nothing to do with redstone: a creeper standing on a powered block still reads 0.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_pregnant
queries.summary: Whether the entity is carrying eggs or young after breeding
queries.hover:
1 from a breeding that makes the entity pregnant until it lays its egg, else 0.
Also set by the `minecraft:is_pregnant` component; saved with the entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is pregnant: after a breeding that causes pregnancy (vanilla turtles) and until the entity has laid its egg. Otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is pregnant and `0` otherwise.

There are three ways the state is switched on:

- **Breeding.** When two entities breed and their breeding setup causes pregnancy (as the vanilla turtle's does), the parent becomes pregnant instead of a baby appearing straight away.
- **The `minecraft:is_pregnant` component.** Adding it turns the state on; removing it turns it off.
- **Loading.** The state is saved with the entity and restored when the world loads.

It is switched off when the entity lays its egg through the egg-laying behavior (`minecraft:behavior.lay_egg`). An entity that is pregnant but has no egg-laying behavior stays pregnant.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities that breed with pregnancy or have minecraft:is_pregnant; others always 0

pitfalls: Without an egg-laying behavior nothing clears the state after breeding - the entity stays pregnant until its component group changes.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_ram_attacking
queries.summary: Whether the entity is charging in a ram attack (goat)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is charging at its target with `minecraft:behavior.ram_attack`, else 0.
On from the moment it stops to line up (head lowered) through the charge; off before that and after the hit.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is charging in a ram attack driven by `minecraft:behavior.ram_attack`, as goats do, and 0 otherwise.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is performing the charge of a ram attack and `0` otherwise.

Only `minecraft:behavior.ram_attack` sets this state. The behavior first walks the entity to a spot at ramming distance from its target; that approach reads `0`. When it gets there and the target is still in place, the entity stops and lowers its head to line up, and the state turns on already at this point - for a goat about a second of standing still before it starts running. It stays on while it accelerates into the charge and turns off when the charge ends - at the hit, when it runs its course, or when the behavior stops. Reloading the entity also clears it.

Entities without that behavior always read `0`.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:behavior.ram_attack; others always 0

timing.updates: per tick while the behavior runs

pitfalls: It is not only the charge: the standing, head-lowered wind-up already reads 1. Only the walk to the ramming spot before it reads 0.
It can drop back to 0 while the entity is still moving fast - at the moment of impact, not when it has come to a stop.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_resting
queries.summary: Whether the entity is resting (a bat hanging, a pet asleep with its owner)
queries.hover:
1 while the entity rests: a bat hanging upside down, or a pet asleep on its owner's bed, else 0.
Bats start out resting when they spawn and wake when hurt.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is resting - a bat hanging from a ceiling, or a tamed pet asleep with its owner - and 0 otherwise.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is resting and `0` otherwise.

Two things set this state:

- **Bats.** A bat is resting while it hangs from a block. A newly created bat starts out resting; its own AI then wakes it or lets it settle depending on the block above it and nearby players, and taking damage wakes it at once. A bat hanging under a ceiling stays resting in daylight too, as long as no player comes close. The state is saved with the bat.
- **Pets sleeping with their owner** (`minecraft:behavior.pet_sleep_with_owner`, used by cats): resting is switched on when the pet lies down on the owner's bed and off when it gets up.

No component turns it on for other entities, so they read `0`.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: bats and pets using minecraft:behavior.pet_sleep_with_owner; others always 0

pitfalls: For a sleeping player use `query.is_sleeping`; resting is only the bat / pet state.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_riding
queries.summary: Whether the entity is riding another entity
queries.hover:
1 while the entity sits on another entity (mob, boat, minecart, ...), else 0.
Checks only that there is a vehicle; use `query.is_riding_any_entity_of_type` for which one.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is riding another entity of any kind - a mob, a boat or a minecart - and 0 otherwise.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity has a vehicle and `0` otherwise.

Any vehicle counts: a player on a horse or pig, a mob sitting in a boat or minecart, a baby zombie on a chicken, a parrot on a player's shoulder. Only the entity's own link to its vehicle is checked; the query says nothing about what kind of vehicle it is or whether the rider controls it.

The riding link is synchronised to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang agree. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: any entity

pitfalls: The vehicle side is `query.has_rider`; `query.is_riding` on the horse itself is 0.

verification.label: Documented for 1.26.60.22; a plain flag or copy with nothing to measure in game

queries.name: is_riding_any_entity_of_type
queries.summary: Whether the entity's vehicle has one of the given entity type ids
queries.hover:
`q.is_riding_any_entity_of_type('minecraft:boat', ...)` - 1 if the entity's direct vehicle has one of the listed type ids, else 0.
Ids need the namespace and must match exactly (`'boat'` never matches).
Arguments are only checked while riding: a non-string argument logs an error then, and is silent otherwise.
queries.description: Returns 1 when the entity is riding an entity whose type id is one of the strings given, and 0 otherwise. At least one string argument is required.
queries.long:
Returns `1` when the entity's vehicle has one of the type ids listed in the arguments, and `0` otherwise.

**What is compared.** The vehicle's type id in the form `namespace:name` (for example `minecraft:chest_boat`), without any spawn event. Each argument is compared with it exactly - letter case, namespace and spelling must match. `'boat'` never matches a boat; write `'minecraft:boat'`.

**Only the direct vehicle.** The query looks at the entity the rider sits on, not further down a stack: a zombie riding a chicken that sits in a boat matches `'minecraft:chicken'` but not `'minecraft:boat'`.

**Arguments.** Give one or more strings. The order does not matter and repeats are harmless.

**Errors and silent cases.** Written bare, with no arguments, the query writes a content-log error and returns `0`; empty brackets `()` are not even accepted by the parser. Without an entity, or when the entity is not riding anything, it returns `0` without evaluating the arguments at all - so a wrong argument goes unnoticed until the entity actually rides something. Once it does, every argument is evaluated, and any argument that is not a string (a number, for example) writes a content-log error and makes the query return `0`, even if another argument matched.

args.name: identifier
args.description: Entity type id with namespace; repeat for more types
accepts: one or more; order and duplicates do not matter
args.onInvalid: no arguments: content-log error, returns 0; a non-string argument while riding: content-log error, returns 0

appliesTo.entities: any entity

whenUnavailable.when: entity is not riding (arguments not evaluated)
riding, and an argument is not a string
riding, no argument matches the vehicle's type id

pitfalls: Leaving out the namespace silently never matches: `q.is_riding_any_entity_of_type('boat')` is always 0.
Boats and chest boats are different types; list both, as vanilla does.
An argument error only shows up while the entity is riding - test the expression with a mounted entity.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

queries.name: is_rising
queries.summary: Old name for query.timer_flag_2 (deprecated)
queries.hover:
Same value as `query.timer_flag_2`: 1 while `minecraft:behavior.timer_flag_2` is running, else 0.
Deprecated: files with a Molang version of 1.20.50 or newer cannot use it.
queries.description: Deprecated. Returns the same value as `query.timer_flag_2`: 1 while the entity's `minecraft:behavior.timer_flag_2` is running, otherwise 0.
queries.long:
Deprecated name for `query.timer_flag_2`. It returns `1` while the entity's `minecraft:behavior.timer_flag_2` behavior is running and `0` otherwise.

**Version gate.** The query only resolves in files whose Molang version is below 1.20.50. In newer files it is an unknown query. Use `query.timer_flag_2` instead.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities running minecraft:behavior.timer_flag_2; others always 0

timing.updates: on start / stop of the timer behavior

pitfalls: Unusable in current packs: with a Molang version of 1.20.50 or newer the name does not resolve. Replace it with `query.timer_flag_2`.

queries.name: is_roaring
queries.summary: Whether the entity is roaring (warden roar, ravager knockback roar)
queries.hover:
1 while `minecraft:behavior.roar` (warden) or `minecraft:behavior.knockback_roar` (ravager) is running, else 0.
Saved with the entity.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is performing a roar - the warden's roar or the ravager's knockback roar - and 0 otherwise.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is roaring and `0` otherwise.

Two behaviors set the state: `minecraft:behavior.roar` (the warden roaring at a new target) and `minecraft:behavior.knockback_roar` (the ravager's roar that pushes nearby mobs back, which vanilla triggers after the ravager has been stunned). The state turns on when the behavior starts and off when it stops, so it lasts as long as the behavior's configured duration.

The state is saved with the entity. Entities without either behavior always read `0`.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:behavior.roar or minecraft:behavior.knockback_roar; others always 0

timing.updates: on start / stop of the roar behavior

queries.name: is_rolling
queries.summary: Whether the entity is rolling over (panda roll behavior)
queries.hover: 1 while `minecraft:behavior.roll` is running (a panda tumbling), else 0.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is rolling over through `minecraft:behavior.roll`, as pandas do, and 0 otherwise.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is rolling and `0` otherwise.

Only `minecraft:behavior.roll` sets the state: it turns on when the behavior starts a roll and off when the behavior stops. Vanilla uses it for the playful panda's tumble. Entities without the behavior always read `0`.

queries.name: is_saddled
queries.summary: Whether the entity wears a saddle
queries.hover:
1 while the entity is saddled, else 0.
Set by the `minecraft:is_saddled` component, or by a saddle in the first slot of `minecraft:equippable`.
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity has a saddle and 0 otherwise. The saddle state comes from the `minecraft:is_saddled` component or from a saddle in the entity's equipment.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is saddled and `0` otherwise.

The state has two sources:

- **The `minecraft:is_saddled` component.** Adding it turns the state on, removing it turns it off. This is how vanilla mounts get it: pigs and striders, and also horses, donkeys, mules and camels, switch to a component group with this component once saddled.
- **Equipment.** For entities with `minecraft:equippable`, the state is also updated from whether the first equipment slot holds a saddle item: putting a saddle into a horse's or camel's saddle slot turns it on, taking it out turns it off.

The state is also saved with the entity. Entities with neither source always read `0`.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:is_saddled or a saddle in their equippable slot; others always 0

timing.updates: on change of the component or the saddle slot

pitfalls: For your own entities with `minecraft:equippable` alone (no `minecraft:is_saddled` component group), test it in game: only vanilla mounts were checked.

verification.label: Partly verified in game on 1.26.60.22; some cases are not measured yet

Saved with the entity.

queries.name: is_searching
queries.summary: Whether the entity is searching for a dig spot (sniffer)
queries.hover:
1 while `minecraft:behavior.random_search_and_dig` is walking the entity to a spot to dig, else 0.
Turns off when it arrives and the dig starts (not yet verified in game).
queries.description: Returns 1 while the entity is in the searching phase of `minecraft:behavior.random_search_and_dig` - the sniffer walking to a spot - and 0 otherwise.
queries.long:
Returns `1` while the entity is searching and `0` otherwise.

Only `minecraft:behavior.random_search_and_dig` sets the state. When the behavior starts, the entity picks a spot and walks to it with the state on; when it arrives (its path is finished) the state turns off and the digging part begins, which has its own query. Stopping the behavior also clears it. The phase boundaries were only partly checked in game: the searching phase lasted 14 to 21 seconds in three tries, each ending without a dig.

Entities without that behavior always read `0`.

The flag is kept by the server and copied to clients, so behavior-pack and resource-pack Molang read the same value. Any arguments are ignored; without an entity the query returns `0`.

appliesTo.entities: entities with minecraft:behavior.random_search_and_dig; others always 0

timing.updates: per tick while the behavior runs
